Exit economics: actual offer value divided by stabilized net operating cash flow, remaining enforceable lease years and net sale proceeds after transfer costs and obligations.
dot_digital_billboard_and_ios_master_lea.name: Digital Billboard Rights and Industrial Outdoor Storage Lease-Spread Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved entitlement and transfer conditions, committed capital before condition satisfaction, occupancy-adjusted rent coverage and buyer-required lease duration versus actual control.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The permit or leasehold cannot be operated or transferred as assumed, leaving the operator with ground-rent obligations and an unsaleable spread.
platform_risks.fallback: Exercise negotiated termination rights before conditions expire, avoid unfunded construction commitments, retain only independently viable permitted operations and pursue a consented alternative use or buyer without assuming the advertised multiple.
platform_risks.impact: Options expire, improvements become stranded, subleasing stops or expected REIT exit value falls substantially.
platform_risks.trigger: DOT spacing conflicts, prohibited digital conversion, IOS zoning restrictions, nontransferable permits, missing landlord consent or a remaining lease term too short for buyer underwriting.

workflow: 1. Screen billboard and IOS opportunities as distinct asset types, verify applicable sign controls or outdoor-storage zoning, and reject sites whose access, spacing, environmental condition or remaining control period defeats the economics.

2. Negotiate conditional options or master leases before major expenditures, expressly allocating permit costs, improvements, restoration duties, assignment rights and any required landlord or agency consent.

3. Obtain required permissions and complete funded improvements, then secure creditworthy advertising or IOS occupancy contracts; test the 2.0x–2.8x IOS rent target after vacancy, operating expenses, reserves and ground-rent escalation.

4. Stabilize collections and prepare a transferable-rights diligence package for qualified buyers, comparing the value of retaining net cash flow against sale proceeds and testing any 16x–22x headline multiple against net income, lease duration and actual bids.

inputs: A documented sourcing ledger identifying the authorized seller, chain of entitlement, event-specific resale and bundling rights, guest-nomination deadlines, transfer windows, and whether each seat, club credential, and parking pass can actually be separated.

A package cost sheet covering the full 16–24-seat suite commitment, independently contracted 4-star room blocks and sprinter capacity, catering minimums, taxes, marketplace commissions, refund exposure, and supplier cancellation schedules.

Executable comparable listings and verified corporate-buyer demand by event, package size, hotel location, and delivery deadline, alongside committed liquidity sufficient to fund purchases and reserves through the expected post-event payout date.
super_bowl_vip_hospitality_allotment_bun.mechanism: Source expressly transferable corporate-sponsor, team/player-family, and official hospitality-partner allotments for Super Bowl, World Cup, F1 Paddock, Masters, and Final Four events; split 16–24-seat stadium suites only where the contract permits individual resale and separately transferable VIP club or parking privileges. Combine eligible seats with contracted 4-star hotel rooms and sprinter transport, calculating net margin after acquisition, fulfillment, marketplace fees, expected unsold-inventory markdowns or write-offs, and cancellation reserves rather than treating the package markup as profit. Model post-event settlement float separately as working capital locked until payout, with its financing cost charged against margin and cash reserved for supplier deadlines and buyer refunds.
metrics: Realized contribution margin per package and per committed suite = collected revenue minus inventory basis, hotel and transport costs, marketplace fees, applicable taxes, fulfillment costs, unsold-inventory losses, cancellation losses or outstanding reserves, and float financing costs.

Sell-through and residual exposure at 30, 14, 7, and 2 days before the event, including unsold suite-seat basis, nonrefundable hotel commitments, and the discount needed to liquidate remaining permitted inventory.
Peak cash tied up and days from supplier payment to cleared marketplace payout, measured against available liquidity and separately maintained cancellation and refund reserves.
super_bowl_vip_hospitality_allotment_bun.name: Super Bowl, Tentpole Sports & Luxury Suite Seat-Splitting Hospitality Arbitrage

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of advertised components with verified written transfer rights and confirmed delivery paths; require 100% before listing.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A sourced allotment cannot be subdivided or transferred with the hospitality privileges advertised.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected listings, retain or return inventory under the supplier agreement, and offer a buyer-accepted authorized replacement or the required refund; unwind refundable ancillary bookings.
platform_risks.impact: Listing removal, failed fulfillment, replacement purchases, buyer refunds, and stranded hotel or transport commitments can eliminate the expected margin.
platform_risks.trigger: Rights-holder restrictions, missed guest-nomination deadlines, or separate club and parking entitlements invalidate the proposed package.

workflow: 1. Obtain written resale, subdivision, and package permissions from the relevant rights holder; exclude nontransferable sponsor or player-family allocations, restricted Masters credentials, and hospitality access that cannot travel with the advertised seat.

2. Underwrite each package using achievable transaction prices, channel-specific fees, conservative sell-through, residual-seat liquidation values, cancellation reserves, and the financing cost of delayed settlement; prefer refundable holds or consignment where available.

3. Publish only confirmed transferable components with explicit inclusions, seat locations, guest-name deadlines, substitution terms, and refund treatment; match corporate orders to the suite manifest and contracted hotel and transport capacity.

4. Reprice remaining inventory at predetermined demand checkpoints, complete permitted ticket and hospitality delivery, reconcile supplier performance and marketplace payouts, and release reserves only after the relevant refund and dispute exposure ends.

inputs: Team and account documents specifying SSL/PSL ownership or permitted use, transfer charges, renewal obligations, resale restrictions, postseason eligibility, allocation limits, purchase deadlines, and any mandatory playoff-strip commitments.

Game-level acquisition and sales data for NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLS seats, including marquee matchup depth, comparable completed sales where available, low-demand liquidation estimates, and account-specific StageFront/Lysted consignment fees and payout terms.

A scenario model separating regular-season face basis, license capital, postseason exercise funding, qualification and allocation probabilities, cancellation reserves, unsold-game losses, and cash availability through post-event settlement.
nfl_nba_ssl_season_strip_playoff_option_.mechanism: Underwrite transferable NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLS season-ticket strips and eligible StageFront/Lysted consignment portfolios, treating marquee-game recovery of 90%–105% of regular-season face basis as a screening hypothesis to verify rather than an assumed outcome. Calculate net margin after marketplace and consignment fees, license acquisition or amortization, mandatory purchases, unsold low-demand inventory slippage, and cancellation reserves; count face-value playoff or championship purchase rights only when the actual account agreement provides them, recognizing that some allocations are lotteries or exclude neutral-site finals. Separate the contingent allocation's probability-weighted value from realized regular-season proceeds, and fund post-event settlement float and playoff exercise deadlines without assuming pending payouts are available cash.
metrics: Marquee recovery ratio = net marquee-game proceeds after selling and consignment fees divided by regular-season face basis; report the 90%–105% screening band separately from whole-portfolio profitability.

Full-season realized contribution after license amortization, acquisition and transfer costs, selling fees, unsold-game write-offs, postseason purchases, cancellation losses or outstanding reserves, and financing costs.

Postseason funding coverage = cleared cash available for exercise divided by contractual postseason payment obligations, paired with probability-weighted allocation value and days until regular-season payouts clear.
nfl_nba_ssl_season_strip_playoff_option_.name: Franchise SSL/PSL Season-Strip & Contingent Playoff Allocation Arbitrage

platform_risks.detection_metric: Share of modeled postseason value supported by current contractual rights, plus unfunded mandatory purchase exposure and days remaining before each exercise deadline.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The anticipated postseason option is absent, restricted, or withdrawn while the operator remains committed to season inventory.
platform_risks.fallback: Assign zero value to unsupported allocations, retain funding for binding obligations, and liquidate eligible regular-season inventory through permitted channels without advertising unconfirmed postseason seats.
platform_risks.impact: Projected option value disappears, mandatory purchases may remain payable, and the regular-season portfolio must stand on its own economics.
platform_risks.trigger: Account-specific allocation rules, missed renewal or exercise deadlines, resale-policy enforcement, nonqualification, or championship access governed by a separate lottery.

workflow: 1. Verify ownership, permitted resale, license obligations, and the precise postseason rights attached to each account; reject portfolios whose valuation depends on unconfirmed championship access or prohibited account transfers.

2. Test whether conservative net marquee-game proceeds can recover 90%–105% of regular-season face basis, then deduct the remaining portfolio costs and stress-test missed playoffs, weak opponents, late schedule changes, and reduced resale demand.

3. Acquire qualifying strips or execute documented consignment mandates, list each seat through one authoritative inventory ledger, and reserve enough cleared cash for mandatory postseason purchases and potential refunds.

4. Monetize marquee games against the recovery plan, mark down weaker games before liquidity deteriorates, exercise only supported and economically justified optional allocations, and reconcile every game's net payout against the full-season basis.

inputs: An owned or expressly consigned inventory ledger with unique event-section-row-seat identifiers, acquisition provenance, purchase-limit compliance, transfer eligibility, delivery deadlines, and confirmed issuer-supported SafeTix transfer capabilities.

Verified account-level exchange integrations and commercial terms covering commissions, listing eligibility, order confirmation, hold and deletion acknowledgments, cancellation and replacement penalties, and post-event settlement schedules.

A pricing and liquidity dataset containing comparable asks and available transaction evidence, inventory age, seat-quality adjustments, time-to-event, demand indicators, minimum net recovery thresholds, reserve balances, and available working capital.
multi_exchange_pos_broadcast_drop_curve_.mechanism: Use supported, authorized SkyBox/Automatiq integrations to broadcast legitimately acquired live-event inventory across eligible StubHub, Vivid Seats, SeatGeek, TickPick, GameTime, and Ticketmaster Resale channels, respecting purchase limits and access controls under the BOTS Act. Capture channel-specific demand with pre-event drop-curve markdowns, measuring net margin after acquisition and marketplace fees, expected unsold-inventory slippage, cancellation reserves, and financing costs while tracking post-event settlement float separately. Use immediate internal POS auto-holds and verified cross-channel delisting to reduce rather than guarantee elimination of double sales, validate any claimed 200% penalty against the applicable contract, and deliver SafeTix inventory through issuer-supported transfer and wallet flows rather than copied rotating barcodes.
metrics: Realized net contribution by exchange and event after acquisition basis, marketplace and automation fees, unsold-inventory write-offs, cancellation or replacement losses and outstanding reserves, and settlement-float financing costs.
Median and 99th-percentile order-to-hold and cross-channel delisting acknowledgment latency, alongside stale-listing counts, overlapping confirmed orders, and actual contract-based penalty exposure.
Sell-through and net recovery by time-to-event pricing checkpoint, paired with forecast-versus-actual markdown losses, peak unsettled receivables, and days from sale to cleared payout.
multi_exchange_pos_broadcast_drop_curve_.name: SkyBox/Automatiq Multi-Exchange POS Broadcast & Dynamic Drop-Curve Arbitrage

platform_risks.detection_metric: Any duplicate seat-level order, unresolved delisting acknowledgment, or synchronization delay beyond the channel-specific tested threshold.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A delayed exchange update permits two buyers to purchase the same seat before all listings are removed.
platform_risks.fallback: Pause broadcasting affected inventory, remove residual listings through authorized account interfaces, contact the exchanges promptly, and resolve duplicate obligations using permitted equivalent replacements or the required cancellation process.
platform_risks.impact: Duplicate fulfillment obligations create replacement-ticket costs, contractual penalties that may reach 200% under some terms, withheld payouts, or account restrictions.
platform_risks.trigger: Concurrent checkout, stale inventory feeds, connector outages, missed order notifications, or unacknowledged hold and delisting requests.

workflow: 1. Connect only supported and authorized exchange accounts, normalize seat identifiers, test order and cancellation synchronization, and keep inventory off any channel whose listing or fulfillment rules cannot be satisfied.

2. Broadcast confirmed inventory with channel-specific fee-adjusted prices; on the first actionable order signal, place an immediate internal hold, request removal elsewhere, and monitor acknowledgments because exchange updates are not atomic.

3. Apply scheduled and demand-triggered markdowns as the event approaches, enforcing net-recovery floors and bounded price changes; isolate stale feeds and require an explicit operator decision before any below-floor liquidation.

4. Fulfill through the issuer's permitted transfer process, monitor acceptance and delivery deadlines, reconcile exchange settlements, and maintain cancellation and replacement reserves until the applicable exposure has ended.

inputs: Importer authorization, importer-of-record identifiers, ACE entry and liquidation extracts, Form 7501 line detail, duty-payment evidence, and existing drawback or protest histories; commercial manifests supply leads rather than proof of eligibility.

Export bills of lading, AES/ITN records where applicable, inventory and manufacturing records, destruction documentation, transfer certificates, and evidence establishing the claimant's rights without duplicate recovery.

Broker and trade-counsel engagements, provision-specific eligibility and deadline matrix, duty-type exclusions, claimant contingency terms, and an itemized budget for historical-data extraction, evidence reconstruction, and filing.
cbp_duty_drawback_and_tariff_protest_con.mechanism: Match ImportGenius/Panjiva shipment leads to importer-authorized ACE entry summaries, CBP Form 7501 data, and export or supervised-destruction evidence; 19 U.S.C. § 1313 generally permits recovery of up to 99% of eligible duties, taxes, and fees, subject to the selected drawback provision's matching, timing, and documentary requirements. Licensed 19 CFR Part 111 customs brokers perform reserved customs business and trade counsel handles legal positions, while the desk separates drawback from § 1514 protests, generally due within 180 days of liquidation or another protestable decision, and excludes antidumping/countervailing duties and other expressly ineligible assessments rather than treating all tariffs as recoverable. Target a 25%–35% contingency only on realized CBP Treasury refunds under contracts permitted for the service provider, with broker/counsel compensation separately structured to avoid prohibited unlicensed customs business or referral-fee sharing and with document reconstruction, filing, and professional costs disclosed separately from gross claims.
metrics: Supported collectible base: eligible paid duties, taxes, and fees multiplied by the applicable recovery percentage, less prior recoveries and unsupported amounts; report manifest-derived opportunities separately.
Cash economics: realized Treasury refunds, contingency receipts at 25%–35%, importer net recovery after disclosed costs, and desk contribution after evidence-acquisition and servicing expense.
Execution quality: percentage of claims with complete entry-to-disposition evidence, days remaining to each statutory deadline, refund realization rate, and post-payment adjustment exposure.
cbp_duty_drawback_and_tariff_protest_con.name: Five-Year CBP ACE Duty-Drawback and Tariff-Protest Recovery Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Unsupported claimed dollars divided by proposed claim dollars, duplicate-entry incidence, and unresolved evidence exceptions before filing.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Manifest matching produces an apparently valuable claim that lacks eligible duties, claimant rights, or auditable export/destruction linkage.
platform_risks.fallback: Remove unsupported lines, pursue only independently timely and supportable alternatives through the broker or counsel, and stop reconstruction when expected net recovery no longer covers its cost.
platform_risks.impact: CBP denies or reduces recovery, reconstruction costs become unrecoverable, and paid accelerated drawback may require repayment with additional consequences.
platform_risks.trigger: ACE reconciliation reveals excluded assessments, substitution-rule failures, duplicate claims, missing transfer records, or an expired filing window.

workflow: 1. Obtain importer permission and reconcile manifest leads to paid ACE entries; segregate eligible duty components, potential drawback provisions, § 1514 issues, and entries already refunded, claimed, protested, or outside the relevant deadline.

2. Have the licensed broker and trade counsel validate direct-identification or substitution requirements, export/destruction timing, claimant rights, and required privileges or notices; generally track export/destruction within five years of importation and complete drawback filing within five years of export/destruction, subject to the applicable provision.

3. Build an entry-to-export or destruction evidence ledger, price unresolved documentation gaps, and submit supported claims or timely protests through the authorized professional without using a protest to bypass an expired statutory claim route.

4. Reconcile Treasury receipts, offsets, claim reductions, accelerated-payment exposure, and final liquidation; invoice the agreed percentage only against realized refunds and maintain records and reserves for audit adjustments or repayment.

inputs: Importer-authorized ACE entry-line exports, original classifications and preference claims, liquidation dates, invoices, product specifications, composition and use evidence, and actual duty payments.

Relevant CROSS decisions and their modification or revocation history, HTSUS legal notes and applicable interpretive rules, and USMCA or other FTA certifications supported by production and origin records.

Licensed-broker and trade-counsel engagements, entry-specific PSC/protest/FTA deadline calendar, prior-refund ledger, and quoted costs for technical analysis, origin substantiation, translations, and filing.
hts_cross_ruling_reclassification_and_ps.mechanism: Audit import lines against the HTSUS, product specifications, CBP CROSS rulings, and agreement-specific origin evidence, recognizing that another importer's published ruling is persuasive only to the extent its facts and legal analysis fit and does not itself bind CBP for this importer. Licensed customs brokers and trade counsel select the available route: an ACE Post-Summary Correction for eligible unliquidated entries, a timely § 1514 protest for protestable liquidation errors, or a qualifying § 1520(d) post-importation preference claim generally filed within one year of importation for an agreement covered by that statute, including USMCA. The collectible base is supported historical overpayment actually refundable through the selected route, net of offsets and professional/documentation costs; prospective landed-cost savings remain a separate forecast and never count as collected refunds.
metrics: Historical recovery funnel: identified overpayment, legally reachable and evidence-supported refund base, accepted adjustments, and realized Treasury receipts after offsets.
Net recovery efficiency: collected refunds less broker, counsel, origin-documentation, and desk charges, with servicing hours and acquisition costs per recovered dollar.
Prospective performance: verified duty-rate change and realized savings on subsequent imports, reported separately from retroactive refunds and from untested volume forecasts.
hts_cross_ruling_reclassification_and_ps.name: CBP CROSS HTS Reclassification, PSC and FTA Retroactive-Refund Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of proposed refund dollars lacking verified product facts, current legal support, origin substantiation, or a valid filing route.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A superficially similar CROSS ruling or incomplete origin certification supports an invalid refund position.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported positions, preserve independently valid timely claims, retain the supported classification, and obtain additional technical evidence or a prospective binding ruling before changing future treatment.
platform_risks.impact: Refunds are denied, future entries may be underpaid, and the importer incurs amendment, assessment, and professional-review costs.
platform_risks.trigger: Technical review finds materially different product facts, a revoked ruling, unmet origin requirements, or an entry outside the chosen correction or claim window.

workflow: 1. Reconcile paid entry lines to liquidation status and product facts; estimate historical overpayment separately from future import-volume savings and exclude entries with duplicate recovery or no remaining statutory route.

2. Have the broker and counsel test the proposed classification against HTSUS text, legal notes, and factually relevant CROSS rulings; verify agreement-specific origin rules rather than relying on a supplier certificate alone.

3. Submit an eligible PSC generally within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline comes first, a timely § 1514 protest where appropriate, or a complete qualifying § 1520(d) claim within its one-year importation deadline; verify current ACE restrictions and do not substitute one route for another's expired deadline.

4. Reconcile liquidation changes and actual Treasury payments to each entry, deduct agreed recovery costs, and separately implement supported classifications or seek a prospective binding ruling for future entries without counting projected savings as refund cash.

inputs: Provider-authorized 835 ERA and 837 claim data, initial-payment or denial receipt dates, payer explanations, QPA disclosures, service codes, facility status, network status, and patient cost-sharing allocations under appropriate privacy and security agreements.

Plan funding and ERISA information, applicable state payment-dispute rules, emergency or nonemergency NSA eligibility facts, notice-and-consent records where relevant, and existing negotiation, IDR, or settlement histories.

Authorized-representative and counsel arrangements, current CMS procedures and certified-entity fee schedules, permissible batching criteria, negotiation/filing calendar, and a collection-based contingency agreement defining QPA and initial-payment treatment.
nsa_federal_idr_batch_arbitration_contin.mechanism: Ingest commercial out-of-network 835 ERA remittances for emergency, anesthesia, radiology, and eligible specialty surgical services, then screen federal No Surprises Act eligibility under 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 and related provider provisions against specified state-law or All-Payer Model rules; ERISA status is relevant but does not alone resolve jurisdiction. An authorized representative, with counsel where legal representation requires it, starts open negotiation within the applicable 30-business-day initiation window, completes the 30-business-day negotiation period, and initiates federal IDR within four business days afterward, batching only disputes that satisfy then-current federal criteria through a certified IDR entity. Charge 20%–30% only on incremental payer cash collected above the contractual QPA floor after nonreimbursed federal administrative and certified-entity fees, also excluding the initial payer payment from new recovery because QPA is a statutory benchmark rather than necessarily the initial payment; track evidence preparation and professional costs separately from submitted offers and awards.
metrics: Collectible dispute base: federally eligible disputed dollars with timely negotiation and IDR rights, separated from billed charges, requested offers, and unpaid awards.

Realized economics: incremental cash above both the initial-payment baseline and contractual QPA floor, net unreimbursed process fees, 20%–30% contingency receipts, and contribution after evidence and representative costs.
Process performance: timely initiation rate, eligible-batch acceptance rate, cost per resolved claim, days from determination to payment, and unpaid-award aging.
nsa_federal_idr_batch_arbitration_contin.name: Federal No Surprises Act Open-Negotiation and Certified-IDR Recovery Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Eligibility rejection rate, batch-separation rate, missed-deadline count, and nonreimbursed process cost as a percentage of incremental collections.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Jurisdiction, batching, or timing defects make an apparently profitable federal IDR submission ineligible.
platform_risks.fallback: Separate disputes only where still timely and permitted, use the applicable state process when available, continue permissible payer negotiation, and cease fee-generating submissions with negative expected net recovery.
platform_risks.impact: Disputes are dismissed or delayed, administrative and preparation expenses are stranded, and an award forecast never becomes incremental provider cash.
platform_risks.trigger: State-law review displaces federal IDR, services fail NSA eligibility, a batch violates current criteria, or negotiation and initiation timestamps miss applicable business-day deadlines.

workflow: 1. Reconcile each ERA to its underlying claim and initial-payment or denial receipt date; exclude ineligible services, route disputes governed by applicable state processes appropriately, and verify federal jurisdiction without assuming every ERISA or specialty-surgery claim qualifies.

2. Send the required open-negotiation notice within 30 business days after receipt of initial payment or denial, run the 30-business-day negotiation period, and assemble permissible evidence without using billed charges or prohibited public-payer comparisons.

3. Initiate federal IDR within four business days after negotiation ends, subject to applicable exceptions or extensions; form only currently permissible batches, select a certified entity, and meet offer, fee, and evidence deadlines rather than treating the initiation window as blanket batching authority.

4. Track settlements, determinations, payer payment deadlines, and actual deposits; calculate the fee base as max(0, cumulative comparable payer cash minus max(initial payer payment, contract-defined comparable QPA floor) minus nonreimbursed administrative and certified-entity fees), excluding patient collections and invoicing only after cash arrives.

inputs: Executed MSO service agreements or verified Arizona ABS licensing documents, state-specific ethics review, fixed/cost-plus rate cards, approved advertising materials, vendor contracts, and an allocation of clinical, legal, and administrative responsibilities.

Documented claimant permission, minimum necessary identifying data, authorized Lexis access and permitted-purpose verification, restricted SSN matching where justified, existing-client indexes, and secure duplicate-review procedures.

Valid patient access requests or medical-record authorizations, provider and EHR inventories, delivery instructions, applicable record-fee rules, privacy/security agreements where required, and a cost ledger for retrieval, processing, and human review.
aba_compliant_law_firm_mso_and_hitech_em.mechanism: Operate a non-lawyer Management Services Organization furnishing fixed or documented cost-plus marketing, intake administration, duplicate-claimant screening, and medical-record retrieval, while the law firm retains client selection, legal advice, litigation judgment, and settlement control under applicable state versions of ABA Model Rule 5.4 and related advertising and solicitation rules. Alternatively, participate through an actually licensed Arizona Alternative Business Structure within its authorized scope, rather than assuming an Arizona license overrides restrictions in other jurisdictions; non-lawyer MSO compensation must not become impermissible legal-fee sharing or payment for recommendations. Retrieve electronic records under valid patient requests or authorizations and 45 CFR § 164.524 as applicable, distinguishing individual-access fee limits from third-party requests whose treatment differs under HITECH and subsequent case law; the collectible base is earned contractual service fees actually paid, not projected settlements, with record-copying, identity-verification, security, and professional-review costs separately accounted for.
metrics: Collected service economics: paid fixed/cost-plus invoices, receivables aging, and contribution after record charges, identity checks, licensed data access, security, and review labor.
Triage quality: confirmed duplicate rate, false-positive rate after human review, source-linked record completeness, and percentage of files requiring additional patient authorization.
Operational integrity: request-to-record turnaround, overdue access requests, unauthorized-access incidents, and compensation exceptions linked to referrals, settlements, or legal-fee percentages.
aba_compliant_law_firm_mso_and_hitech_em.name: Rule 5.4-Aligned Law-Firm MSO and Patient-Directed Electronic-Records Triage Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of contracts with outcome-linked compensation, unauthorized legal-decision exceptions, jurisdictional licensing gaps, and record requests missing verified authority.
platform_risks.failure_mode: An administrative services arrangement drifts into prohibited fee sharing, paid recommendations, unauthorized legal practice, or unauthorized health-record access.
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend the affected activity, refer legal decisions to licensed counsel, correct pricing and marketing under ethics review, restrict improperly obtained records, and resume only services supported by valid contracts, permissions, and jurisdictional authority.
platform_risks.impact: The law firm and operator face disciplinary, licensing, privacy, contractual, and collection exposure, while affected records and invoices may require remediation.
platform_risks.trigger: Compensation becomes settlement-linked, marketing promises legal outcomes, staff make legal eligibility decisions, Arizona licensing is treated as nationwide permission, or records are requested without a valid authority pathway.

workflow: 1. Choose and document the operating structure with qualified ethics counsel: use a fixed/cost-plus MSO without prohibited ownership or fee sharing, or obtain the required Arizona ABS license before operating as one; review every jurisdiction served and preserve lawyers' independent judgment.

2. Run approved marketing and administrative intake without selling legal recommendations or making merits determinations; match permitted claimant identifiers against authorized internal and Lexis records, minimize SSN exposure, and send possible duplicates or conflicts to the firm's designated reviewer.

3. Submit properly scoped patient requests or authorizations and distinguish patient access from third-party disclosure pathways; apply the relevant fee rules and, for requests governed by § 164.524, track its 30-calendar-day response period and permitted single extension with written notice, while checking shorter applicable state deadlines.

4. Deduplicate and organize received records into source-linked timelines for lawyer review, restrict access and retention, and invoice documented fixed or cost-plus services independently of settlement size, legal fees, or outcome; reconcile service payments against actual delivery costs.

inputs: Parcel ownership, title exceptions, zoning, access and easement records; utility headroom publications and transmission GIS; fiber-provider route information with written confirmation of serviceability, route diversity, construction cost, and delivery timing.

Project-specific electrical envelopes covering BESS charging and export MW, duration and dispatch constraints, or AI firm load, ramp profile, redundancy, cooling and water requirements; utility study procedures, queue data, upgrade-cost estimates, and written capacity and timing evidence.

Landowner option templates specifying premium, exercise price, 12–24 month term, extensions, assignment consent, diligence termination rights, access for testing, and treatment of deposits; Phase I environmental assessments, wetland delineation needs, floodplain screens, and a qualified developer buyer list.
bess_and_modular_ai_substation_land_opti.mechanism: Overlay utility hosting-capacity maps, 69–345 kV transmission corridors, dark-fiber routes, and environmental constraints to originate expressly assignable, diligence-contingent 12–24 month land options. Hosting-capacity maps and proximity are prospecting signals, not commitments: value each option strictly against utility-validated deliverable MW, project-specific import/export requirements, network-upgrade exposure, and a realistic energization schedule. Monetize documented site-control assignments to qualified BESS or modular AI developers, with separate treatment of land rights, interconnection rights, and any utility consent required for a project transfer.
metrics: Risk-adjusted assignment margin = contracted assignment proceeds minus option premiums, extensions, studies, environmental work, legal costs, transaction costs, and probability-weighted failed-site spend; report cash at risk before any buyer payment.

Utility-validated usable MW by import/export service condition, supporting evidence stage, and expected energization date; track the percentage of screened capacity surviving studies rather than presenting map headroom as saleable capacity.
Site conversion and timing: screened parcels to signed options to paid assignments, months of option term remaining beyond expected diligence, and upgrade-cost sensitivity per usable MW.
bess_and_modular_ai_substation_land_opti.name: Utility-Validated BESS and Modular AI Land-Option Origination Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Track variance between preliminary and studied MW, upgrade estimates, and energization dates, plus remaining option months relative to utility study and permitting milestones.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Indicative utility headroom is mistaken for deliverable service, leaving an option on land that cannot support the buyer's operating profile within the option term.
platform_risks.fallback: Use the contractual diligence exit or renegotiate price and term before further nonrefundable spending; pursue an alternative operating profile only after fresh utility validation, and withdraw unsupported capacity claims from buyer materials.
platform_risks.impact: The assignment value falls sharply while option premiums, engineering costs, and extension payments become stranded; a land assignment may also fail to preserve separately governed interconnection rights.
platform_risks.trigger: A utility study identifies binding thermal or voltage constraints, a competing service request consumes available capacity, or required upgrades move energization beyond the buyer's investment horizon.

workflow: 1. Rank parcels using corridor, substation, fiber, access, zoning, and environmental overlays; distinguish distribution hosting estimates from transmission deliverability and exclude sites whose apparent capacity depends on unsupported map interpretation.

2. Obtain project-specific utility feedback on import and export capacity, operating restrictions, study requirements, interconnection facilities, upgrades, and achievable energization dates; label screening feedback separately from completed studies and executable service commitments.

3. Execute a counsel-reviewed, expressly assignable 12–24 month option with environmental and utility diligence contingencies, staged payments, extension economics, and clear exercise mechanics; commission Phase I work and necessary wetlands, title, access, and permitting investigations before additional capital becomes nonrefundable.

4. Market a version-controlled diligence package to qualified developers, price the assignment using utility-validated usable MW and schedule-adjusted developer economics, and close through documented assignment and escrow procedures; verify state real-estate licensing rules and separately obtain any required utility or queue-transfer consent.

inputs: Lawfully obtained procurement, payment, grant, corporate-filing, enforcement, and pricing datasets with acquisition dates, source URLs, applicable use rights, immutable snapshots, transformation code, and a documented separation of public records from any authorized nonpublic evidence.

Counsel-defined investigative hypotheses identifying the relevant payment or securities/tax theory, responsible actors, transaction dates, representations, materiality, estimated loss, alternative explanations, and unresolved evidentiary gaps.

Written analytics engagement covering scope, ordinary service fees, conflicts, confidentiality, evidence retention, and ownership; separate counsel assessments of FCA public disclosure, original-source status, first-to-file and limitations issues, SEC original-information requirements, and IRS submission eligibility.
fca_qui_tam_and_sec_whistleblower_forens.mechanism: Sell scoped B2B forensic-analytics retainers to contingency relator firms, producing reproducible evidence packages for potential False Claims Act matters under 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3730 and distinct SEC or IRS whistleblower pathways under 15 U.S.C. § 78u-6 and 26 U.S.C. § 7623. Public-data anomalies alone do not establish a knowingly false, material claim or satisfy Rule 9(b); FCA public-disclosure and original-source analysis differs from the SEC's potential recognition of qualifying independent analysis. Treat service revenue as the operating business and any personally eligible whistleblower award as separate, contingent, potentially multi-year proceeds rather than a purchased claim, promised recovery, or share of counsel's legal fees.
metrics: Collected retainer and milestone revenue minus analyst labor, data licensing, expert review, secure storage, and rework; track receivable days and client concentration without booking speculative awards as earned service revenue.

Evidence quality: reproducible transaction coverage, precision on manually reviewed anomalies, documented alternative explanations, and the share of allegations supported by claim-specific facts rather than aggregate correlations.

Program-specific contingent recovery register: FCA shares generally 15–25% with government intervention or 25–30% without, subject to statutory exceptions; SEC awards generally 10–30% of collected sanctions in qualifying actions exceeding $1 million; IRS § 7623(b) generally 15–30% subject to its monetary, taxpayer-income, and other requirements.
fca_qui_tam_and_sec_whistleblower_forens.name: Public-Data Forensic Analytics and Relator Litigation-Support Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Measure unresolved statutory-element gaps, unsupported claim assertions, source-provenance exceptions, and matters lacking a documented program-specific assessment by counsel.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A compelling statistical pattern is sold as an award-eligible case despite public-disclosure restrictions, insufficient claim-specific facts, or a mismatch between the evidence and the selected whistleblower program.
platform_risks.fallback: Narrow the deliverable to supported forensic findings, preserve exculpatory evidence, and pursue further lawful corroboration only within the engagement; stop unsupported allegations and retain collected service-fee economics separately from any abandoned award thesis.
platform_risks.impact: Dismissal, award denial, wasted litigation expense, confidentiality exposure, and impaired client relationships; paid analytics work does not itself establish relator standing or award eligibility.
platform_risks.trigger: The material is already publicly disclosed or known to authorities, the analyst contributes no qualifying independent analysis or original-source knowledge, or counsel cannot connect anomalies to the required statutory elements.

workflow: 1. Select a narrow, counsel-approved hypothesis and reproduce the underlying transactions from preserved source data; document methodology, false-positive controls, lawful access, and contrary evidence without accessing restricted systems or soliciting privileged material.

2. Build a transaction-level evidence matrix linking alleged conduct to identifiable claims, statements, actors, dates, knowledge indicators, and materiality; have counsel test Rule 9(b) particularity under the governing circuit and assess FCA public-disclosure and original-source issues before characterizing a matter as actionable.

3. Deliver the paid forensic report and reproducible workpapers independently of any award outcome; counsel selects the appropriate pathway, including an FCA complaint initially filed under seal with statutory government disclosures, an SEC TCR submission, or an IRS Form 211, rather than treating the programs as interchangeable.

4. Maintain controlled litigation support, evidence updates, and a docket of counsel-managed deadlines; respect the FCA's initial statutory seal period of at least 60 days and any court-granted extensions, which can extend for years, while forecasting operations from collected retainers rather than expected awards.

inputs: Verified DCM and intermediary status, current contract specifications and rulebooks, settlement sources, dispute provisions, trading hours, market-data licenses, API terms, geographic restrictions, and written builder or referral arrangements where offered.

Timestamped executable bids and offers, displayed depth, trades, venue and intermediary fees, rate limits, account-access architecture, and contract taxonomies that preserve differences in event definitions, observation windows, and settlement rules.

A documented activity analysis covering compensated solicitation, order acceptance or transmission, personalized recommendations, discretionary trading, IB/FCM/CTA requirements and available exemptions; scoped API permissions, consent records, commercial disclosures, and an explicit prohibition on custody and pooled capital.
cftc_dcm_prediction_market_analytics_and.mechanism: Earn subscriptions from cross-venue probability, settlement-rule, and liquidity analytics for event contracts listed on CFTC Designated Contract Markets such as Kalshi and ForecastEx, using licensed data and venue-authorized access channels. Add builder or referral compensation only where the relevant exchange, intermediary, and applicable registration framework permit the specific activity; non-custody alone does not remove introducing-broker or commodity-trading-advisor obligations. Keep customer funds, positions, margin, and account approval with the authorized venue or intermediary, and use read-only analytics or permitted outbound referrals unless order transmission has a documented lawful operating basis.
metrics: Subscription contribution margin = collected recurring revenue minus licensed data, infrastructure, support, payment processing, and acquisition costs; report referral receipts separately and net of contractual reversals.

Market-data quality: quote age, feed uptime, contract-mapping exception rate, and executable depth at the displayed price; calculate cross-venue spreads after all observable fees and explicit settlement-basis adjustments.

For authorized routing only, user-consented order acceptance rate, execution slippage against the timestamped executable quote, cancellation latency, and reconciliation exceptions; for referrals, verified attributed accounts and realized revenue per eligible referral.
cftc_dcm_prediction_market_analytics_and.name: Regulated Event-Contract Probability Terminal and Permitted Referral Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Track feature and compensation changes against the documented permitted-activity scope, percentage of order endpoints with an established authorization basis, and unresolved venue-term or registration-status exceptions.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A non-custodial analytics product crosses into compensated solicitation, order handling, or advisory activity without the required registration or a valid exemption.
platform_risks.fallback: Disable the affected routing, solicitation, or recommendation feature, preserve records, and continue only the lawfully supported read-only analytics or referral functionality; resume expanded activity through an appropriately registered arrangement or a substantiated exemption.
platform_risks.impact: Routing suspension, terminated commercial agreements, regulatory exposure, customer execution disputes, and loss of referral revenue despite the platform never holding funds.
platform_risks.trigger: A builder integration begins transmitting customer orders, transaction-linked compensation changes the solicitation model, personalized trade recommendations are introduced, or venue and intermediary terms change.

workflow: 1. Confirm each venue's current regulatory status, customer-access model, data rights, and permitted territories; distinguish direct venue access from intermediary access, including ForecastEx access through authorized intermediaries, and verify the current availability of any commercial referral program.

2. Normalize contracts only when their event definitions and settlement mechanics support a meaningful comparison; display bid/ask-derived implied probabilities, depth, timestamps, fees, and settlement differences rather than describing every price spread as executable arbitrage.

3. Launch paid read-only dashboards with stale-data suppression, spread and depth filters, reproducible calculations, and clearly disclosed commercial relationships; assess whether recommendation features create CTA obligations before enabling them.

4. Enable only contractually permitted referral links or a separately authorized routing implementation after documenting the registration or exemption basis; require user-directed orders through the authorized venue or intermediary, minimize token permissions, and retain consent and routing logs without receiving customer funds.

inputs: A current jurisdiction-by-product authorization matrix covering operator licenses, affiliate or vendor requirements, permitted compensation models, marketing restrictions, minimum ages, and Ontario AGCO and iGaming Ontario requirements relevant to each participant's role.

Executed operator agreements defining eligible first-time depositors, identity and location verification, qualifying deposits or wagering, attribution windows, CPA reversals, NGR deductions, revenue-share percentages, negative-carryover scope, payment timing, and audit or reconciliation rights.

Versioned comparison data, operator-confirmed product availability, consent-based attribution, location and age-screening controls, responsible-gambling resources, suppression and self-exclusion handling where applicable, and editorial rules excluding offshore operators and unlawful sweepstakes destinations.
state_licensed_igaming_sportsbook_affili.mechanism: Operate jurisdiction-specific sportsbook and online-casino comparison calculators and matchup hubs that route eligible adults only to operators authorized for the relevant product and location in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Michigan, West Virginia, or Ontario, which is a Canadian province rather than a US state. Earn contractually verified first-time-depositor CPA and, where permitted, negotiated net-gaming-revenue shares after specified bonus, tax, administrative, chargeback, and negative-carryover treatment. Obtain the affiliate, vendor, supplier, or revenue-share permissions actually required in each jurisdiction and commercial arrangement; do not assume one registration covers every market or compensation model.

Realized revenue share = contractual share percentage applied to the eligible NGR base after agreed deductions and carryover treatment; reconcile the opening negative balance, current-period activity, payable amount, and closing balance by contractual reporting unit.

Jurisdiction-level contribution margin and control quality: content and acquisition cost per paid depositor, cash payback period, blocked ineligible-location clicks, age-screening failures, outdated offers, and operator-authorization exceptions.
state_licensed_igaming_sportsbook_affili.name: NJ, PA, MI, WV and Ontario Regulated Gaming Affiliate Comparison Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Monitor restricted-location link exposure, unauthorized destination counts, jurisdiction-specific advertising exceptions, CPA reversal rates, and unexplained differences between internal estimates and operator settlement statements.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A comparison page routes an ineligible visitor or publishes an impermissible promotion, while weak reconciliation overstates earnings from rejected depositors or negative NGR.
platform_risks.fallback: Disable affected offers and monetized links by jurisdiction, preserve relevant records, replace promotional content with permitted factual information, and reconcile or dispute settlement differences through contractual processes; never redirect blocked traffic to offshore operators or unlawful sweepstakes.
platform_risks.impact: Affiliate suspension, withheld commissions, regulatory action, customer harm, and materially lower cash receipts than the portal's gross acquisition dashboard suggests.
platform_risks.trigger: Location cannot be verified, an operator loses or changes authorization, a public Ontario page displays a prohibited inducement, or operator reporting applies unexpected bonus deductions, clawbacks, or carryover.

2. Publish substantiated comparisons and matchup content with prominent affiliate disclosures, clear calculator assumptions, and responsible-gambling information; apply jurisdiction-specific promotion rules, including Ontario restrictions on public advertising of gambling inducements, bonuses, and credits.

Restrict monetized links to eligible locations and products using layered geolocation and fail-closed handling of uncertain location, without offering circumvention instructions; use affiliate age screening while leaving mandatory identity, age, self-exclusion, and wagering-location verification with the authorized operator.

Reconcile operator-confirmed qualifying depositors, duplicate or fraudulent accounts, CPA clawbacks, and contract-defined monthly NGR; account for deductions and negative carryover at the agreed player, brand, product, or portfolio level, and suspend links immediately when authorization or permitted marketing terms change.

TrustedForm or Jornaya records can support evidence of the actual named-recipient disclosure but do not independently establish valid consent; negotiated 90–120-second duration triggers qualify payment only alongside genuine caller intent, buyer acceptance and applicable contract terms.

platform_risks.detection_metric: Consent-recipient mismatch count, complaint and reversal rates by source, and anomalous clustering of call endings immediately after the billing threshold.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A buyer or routing platform rejects calls or suspends the program because consent, marketing representations or traffic quality fails applicable requirements.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected sources and transfers, preserve evidence securely, refund invalid billings and resume only with corrected disclosures, permitted compensation structures and verified buyer acceptance.
platform_risks.impact: Payout reversals, account suspension, consumer complaints and potential regulatory or contractual exposure.

workflow: 1. Approve legitimate traffic sources and buyer contracts, segregate verticals, and establish how each caller receives accurate recipient disclosures without misleading benefit claims or prohibited steering.

2. Screen intent, geography, duplicates and applicable transfer restrictions; obtain required permission before transmitting personal information and send only permitted minimal qualification metadata in bid requests.

3. Run the supported sub-second auction with timeouts and capacity checks, identify the selected recipient and obtain any required recipient-specific permission before transfer, then connect the caller without artificially extending duration.
4. Reconcile buyer acceptance and any 90–120-second billing condition against call records, resolve disputes, suppress invalid sources and settle only genuine, contract-qualified calls.
