plays.mechanism: Source expressly transferable corporate-sponsor, team/player-family, and official hospitality-partner allotments for Super Bowl, World Cup, F1 Paddock, Masters, and Final Four events; split 16–24-seat stadium suites only where the contract permits individual resale and separately transferable VIP club or parking privileges. Combine eligible seats with contracted 4-star hotel rooms and sprinter transport, calculating net margin after acquisition, fulfillment, marketplace fees, expected unsold-inventory markdowns or write-offs, and cancellation reserves rather than treating the package markup as profit. Model post-event settlement float separately as working capital locked until payout, with its financing cost charged against margin and cash reserved for supplier deadlines and buyer refunds.
metrics: Realized contribution margin per package and per committed suite = collected revenue minus inventory basis, hotel and transport costs, marketplace fees, applicable taxes, fulfillment costs, unsold-inventory losses, cancellation losses or outstanding reserves, and float financing costs.

Sell-through and residual exposure at 30, 14, 7, and 2 days before the event, including unsold suite-seat basis, nonrefundable hotel commitments, and the discount needed to liquidate remaining permitted inventory.
Peak cash tied up and days from supplier payment to cleared marketplace payout, measured against available liquidity and separately maintained cancellation and refund reserves.
plays.name: Super Bowl, Tentpole Sports & Luxury Suite Seat-Splitting Hospitality Arbitrage

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of advertised components with verified written transfer rights and confirmed delivery paths; require 100% before listing.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A sourced allotment cannot be subdivided or transferred with the hospitality privileges advertised.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected listings, retain or return inventory under the supplier agreement, and offer a buyer-accepted authorized replacement or the required refund; unwind refundable ancillary bookings.
platform_risks.impact: Listing removal, failed fulfillment, replacement purchases, buyer refunds, and stranded hotel or transport commitments can eliminate the expected margin.
platform_risks.trigger: Rights-holder restrictions, missed guest-nomination deadlines, or separate club and parking entitlements invalidate the proposed package.

workflow: 1. Obtain written resale, subdivision, and package permissions from the relevant rights holder; exclude nontransferable sponsor or player-family allocations, restricted Masters credentials, and hospitality access that cannot travel with the advertised seat.

2. Underwrite each package using achievable transaction prices, channel-specific fees, conservative sell-through, residual-seat liquidation values, cancellation reserves, and the financing cost of delayed settlement; prefer refundable holds or consignment where available.

3. Publish only confirmed transferable components with explicit inclusions, seat locations, guest-name deadlines, substitution terms, and refund treatment; match corporate orders to the suite manifest and contracted hotel and transport capacity.

4. Reprice remaining inventory at predetermined demand checkpoints, complete permitted ticket and hospitality delivery, reconcile supplier performance and marketplace payouts, and release reserves only after the relevant refund and dispute exposure ends.

inputs: Team and account documents specifying SSL/PSL ownership or permitted use, transfer charges, renewal obligations, resale restrictions, postseason eligibility, allocation limits, purchase deadlines, and any mandatory playoff-strip commitments.

Game-level acquisition and sales data for NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLS seats, including marquee matchup depth, comparable completed sales where available, low-demand liquidation estimates, and account-specific StageFront/Lysted consignment fees and payout terms.

A scenario model separating regular-season face basis, license capital, postseason exercise funding, qualification and allocation probabilities, cancellation reserves, unsold-game losses, and cash availability through post-event settlement.
plays.mechanism: Underwrite transferable NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLS season-ticket strips and eligible StageFront/Lysted consignment portfolios, treating marquee-game recovery of 90%–105% of regular-season face basis as a screening hypothesis to verify rather than an assumed outcome. Calculate net margin after marketplace and consignment fees, license acquisition or amortization, mandatory purchases, unsold low-demand inventory slippage, and cancellation reserves; count face-value playoff or championship purchase rights only when the actual account agreement provides them, recognizing that some allocations are lotteries or exclude neutral-site finals. Separate the contingent allocation's probability-weighted value from realized regular-season proceeds, and fund post-event settlement float and playoff exercise deadlines without assuming pending payouts are available cash.
metrics: Marquee recovery ratio = net marquee-game proceeds after selling and consignment fees divided by regular-season face basis; report the 90%–105% screening band separately from whole-portfolio profitability.

Full-season realized contribution after license amortization, acquisition and transfer costs, selling fees, unsold-game write-offs, postseason purchases, cancellation losses or outstanding reserves, and financing costs.

Postseason funding coverage = cleared cash available for exercise divided by contractual postseason payment obligations, paired with probability-weighted allocation value and days until regular-season payouts clear.
plays.name: Franchise SSL/PSL Season-Strip & Contingent Playoff Allocation Arbitrage

platform_risks.detection_metric: Share of modeled postseason value supported by current contractual rights, plus unfunded mandatory purchase exposure and days remaining before each exercise deadline.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The anticipated postseason option is absent, restricted, or withdrawn while the operator remains committed to season inventory.
platform_risks.fallback: Assign zero value to unsupported allocations, retain funding for binding obligations, and liquidate eligible regular-season inventory through permitted channels without advertising unconfirmed postseason seats.
platform_risks.impact: Projected option value disappears, mandatory purchases may remain payable, and the regular-season portfolio must stand on its own economics.
platform_risks.trigger: Account-specific allocation rules, missed renewal or exercise deadlines, resale-policy enforcement, nonqualification, or championship access governed by a separate lottery.

workflow: 1. Verify ownership, permitted resale, license obligations, and the precise postseason rights attached to each account; reject portfolios whose valuation depends on unconfirmed championship access or prohibited account transfers.

2. Test whether conservative net marquee-game proceeds can recover 90%–105% of regular-season face basis, then deduct the remaining portfolio costs and stress-test missed playoffs, weak opponents, late schedule changes, and reduced resale demand.

3. Acquire qualifying strips or execute documented consignment mandates, list each seat through one authoritative inventory ledger, and reserve enough cleared cash for mandatory postseason purchases and potential refunds.

4. Monetize marquee games against the recovery plan, mark down weaker games before liquidity deteriorates, exercise only supported and economically justified optional allocations, and reconcile every game's net payout against the full-season basis.

inputs: An owned or expressly consigned inventory ledger with unique event-section-row-seat identifiers, acquisition provenance, purchase-limit compliance, transfer eligibility, delivery deadlines, and confirmed issuer-supported SafeTix transfer capabilities.

Verified account-level exchange integrations and commercial terms covering commissions, listing eligibility, order confirmation, hold and deletion acknowledgments, cancellation and replacement penalties, and post-event settlement schedules.

A pricing and liquidity dataset containing comparable asks and available transaction evidence, inventory age, seat-quality adjustments, time-to-event, demand indicators, minimum net recovery thresholds, reserve balances, and available working capital.
plays.mechanism: Use supported, authorized SkyBox/Automatiq integrations to broadcast legitimately acquired live-event inventory across eligible StubHub, Vivid Seats, SeatGeek, TickPick, GameTime, and Ticketmaster Resale channels, respecting purchase limits and access controls under the BOTS Act. Capture channel-specific demand with pre-event drop-curve markdowns, measuring net margin after acquisition and marketplace fees, expected unsold-inventory slippage, cancellation reserves, and financing costs while tracking post-event settlement float separately. Use immediate internal POS auto-holds and verified cross-channel delisting to reduce rather than guarantee elimination of double sales, validate any claimed 200% penalty against the applicable contract, and deliver SafeTix inventory through issuer-supported transfer and wallet flows rather than copied rotating barcodes.
metrics: Realized net contribution by exchange and event after acquisition basis, marketplace and automation fees, unsold-inventory write-offs, cancellation or replacement losses and outstanding reserves, and settlement-float financing costs.
Median and 99th-percentile order-to-hold and cross-channel delisting acknowledgment latency, alongside stale-listing counts, overlapping confirmed orders, and actual contract-based penalty exposure.
Sell-through and net recovery by time-to-event pricing checkpoint, paired with forecast-versus-actual markdown losses, peak unsettled receivables, and days from sale to cleared payout.
plays.name: SkyBox/Automatiq Multi-Exchange POS Broadcast & Dynamic Drop-Curve Arbitrage

platform_risks.detection_metric: Any duplicate seat-level order, unresolved delisting acknowledgment, or synchronization delay beyond the channel-specific tested threshold.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A delayed exchange update permits two buyers to purchase the same seat before all listings are removed.
platform_risks.fallback: Pause broadcasting affected inventory, remove residual listings through authorized account interfaces, contact the exchanges promptly, and resolve duplicate obligations using permitted equivalent replacements or the required cancellation process.
platform_risks.impact: Duplicate fulfillment obligations create replacement-ticket costs, contractual penalties that may reach 200% under some terms, withheld payouts, or account restrictions.
platform_risks.trigger: Concurrent checkout, stale inventory feeds, connector outages, missed order notifications, or unacknowledged hold and delisting requests.

workflow: 1. Connect only supported and authorized exchange accounts, normalize seat identifiers, test order and cancellation synchronization, and keep inventory off any channel whose listing or fulfillment rules cannot be satisfied.

2. Broadcast confirmed inventory with channel-specific fee-adjusted prices; on the first actionable order signal, place an immediate internal hold, request removal elsewhere, and monitor acknowledgments because exchange updates are not atomic.

3. Apply scheduled and demand-triggered markdowns as the event approaches, enforcing net-recovery floors and bounded price changes; isolate stale feeds and require an explicit operator decision before any below-floor liquidation.

4. Fulfill through the issuer's permitted transfer process, monitor acceptance and delivery deadlines, reconcile exchange settlements, and maintain cancellation and replacement reserves until the applicable exposure has ended.

plays.name: Multi-Account Presale Code & Limited-Mintage Allocation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Operating hundreds of aged, human-scored 'free' fan-club, ticketing (Ticketmaster Verified Fan / AXS), U.S. Mint, and limited-edition luxury/collectible accounts—each backed by unique residential proxies, aged browser profiles, and virtual card numbers (VCCs)—to multiply lottery/queue odds by 100x–500x on strict 'limit 1–4 per account' releases trading at instant 50–300% secondary-market premiums.
inputs: Aged ticketing, fan-club, and sovereign-mint account fleet with clean purchase histories
Anti-detect browser matrix with residential ISP proxies and unique SIM/SMS verification lines
Corporate virtual credit card (VCC) issuance API (Extend/Ramp/Slash) with distinct billing descriptors
workflow: Monitor upcoming concert tours, playoff games, U.S. Mint numismatic releases, and limited collectible drops with secondary-market spreads >=50%
Register the aged account fleet across presale lotteries and waiting rooms to secure high-priority access codes and low queue positions
Execute checkouts strictly on high-margin allocations (front-row/pit seats, low-mintage proof coins) using isolated VCCs per household profile
Flip allocations immediately via direct consignment, verified ticket exchanges (StubHub/SeatGeek/Vivid API), or pre-committed wholesale buyers
metrics: Presale code / top-1,000 queue-position hit rate (%) across the account cluster
Net realized secondary-market spread (%) after exchange/consignment fees
Inventory hold time (hours/days from checkout to settled resale payout)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Order cancellation or queue-score penalty from device/payment fingerprint linkage
platform_risks.trigger: Reusing identical billing addresses, card BINs, or browser WebGL/Canvas fingerprints across Household-Limit-restricted drops
platform_risks.impact: Canceled orders, revoked presale codes, or permanent account flagging
platform_risks.detection_metric: Post-checkout order survival rate (%) and queue-score tier telemetry
platform_risks.fallback: Maintain genuine distributed buyer consortiums with unique residential addresses, distinct bank BINs, and pre-sold wholesale buyer commitments before checkout

inputs: Verified buying-group identity and operating terms, written purchase orders with fixed SKUs and acceptance criteria, warehouse instructions, settlement obligations and return or rejection allocation.

Commercial card agreements showing authorized use, purchase limits, eligible reward rates and caps, bonus conditions, statement timing, actual payment deadlines and any restrictions on resale purchases.

Supplier availability and invoices, documented resale or exemption eligibility where applicable, shipment insurance and tracking, working-capital reserves and a transaction-level inventory and cash ledger.
plays.mechanism: Fulfill genuine, pre-committed buying-group purchase orders through BuyForMeRetail, Pointsmaker or independently verified counterparties, using authorized commercial card purchases and documented delivery to designated warehouses in Delaware, New Hampshire or Oregon. Earn the contracted merchandise spread plus only eligible 2%–4% cashback or bonus value, using uncapped rewards solely when current issuer terms explicitly provide them; tax treatment depends on sourcing, possession, resale documentation and downstream obligations rather than a tax-free warehouse label. Match a contractually verified Net-3 ACH settlement to the actual card due date, which may provide up to approximately 60 days only on suitable products and purchase dates, without circular purchases, fictitious sales or issuer-limit evasion.
metrics: Realized order contribution: buyer proceeds plus posted eligible rewards minus merchandise, freight, tax, insurance, financing, returns and dispute costs.
Cash-conversion spread: actual card payment due date minus cleared buyer settlement date, with stress tests for late acceptance and ACH reversals.
Exposure control: unsettled counterparty receivables, rejected-unit rate and liquid reserves divided by card obligations due before stressed settlement.
plays.name: Pre-Committed Buying-Group Fulfillment and Commercial Card Working-Capital Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Receivables aging beyond the contractual Net-3 start event, rejected deliveries, reward clawbacks and stressed cash coverage below the operator's minimum.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Buying-group acceptance or settlement fails while the card issuer still requires full repayment or reverses expected rewards.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop new purchases, meet card obligations from reserved cash, recover or resell legitimately owned goods through permitted channels and resume only after settlement reliability and issuer eligibility are confirmed.
platform_risks.impact: A nominally profitable order becomes illiquid inventory and unsecured receivables, with interest charges, lost rewards or restricted card access.
platform_risks.trigger: Counterparty insolvency, SKU rejection, warehouse delivery disputes, delayed ACH, reward exclusions or issuer restrictions on purchase and repayment patterns.

workflow: 1. Verify the counterparty and current BuyForMeRetail or Pointsmaker program terms before funding any order; confirm that the PO is genuinely committed rather than treating an indicative buying list as guaranteed demand.

2. Calculate landed margin after tax, shipping, reward exclusions, returns and financing costs; size purchases to available cash repayment capacity and issuer-approved limits rather than assuming all cards provide uncapped rewards or 60-day float.

3. Purchase approved merchandise and ship to the specifically authorized DE, NH or OR warehouse with chain-of-custody evidence, recording title transfer, acceptance events and the exact event that starts Net-3 settlement.

4. Reconcile accepted units and cleared ACH proceeds, reserve for returns or reversals, pay the statement by its actual due date and fund subsequent genuine orders only within verified counterparty and issuer limits.

plays.name: B2B Commercial Virtual Card (VCC) Interchange & AP Settlement Rebate Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Embedding a 'Free Automated Accounts Payable (AP) / Instant Vendor Settlement' platform inside high-volume B2B verticals (freight brokerage, construction general contracting, medical supply, property management, media agencies) that converts checks and ACH payables into single-use Visa/Mastercard Commercial Virtual Credit Cards (VCCs)—capturing 140–195 basis points (1.40%–1.95%) in uncapped commercial interchange rebates on hundreds of millions in third-party invoice volume.
inputs: BaaS / Commercial Card Issuing bank partnership (Marqeta, Lithic, Stripe Issuing, Highnote, Cross River) on uncapped Visa/Mastercard Large-Ticket & Purchasing interchange tiers
ERP/accounting connector (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, McLeod/TMW freight TMS) ingesting open vendor AP ledgers
Automated vendor-enablement call/email engine pitching 'Day-1 Instant Payment via Virtual Card vs. Net-45 Check/ACH'
workflow: Onboard mid-market companies with $20M–$250M/yr in fragmented vendor payables onto a $0-cost AP automation and working-capital portal
Cross-reference their vendor master list against Visa/Mastercard supplier-acceptance networks to flag vendors that already accept card payments
Offer remaining vendors immediate Day-1 invoice settlement via single-use emailed/API virtual card in exchange for waiving Net-30/Net-60 wait times
Earn 1.50%–1.95% gross interchange rebate from the issuing bank on every settled dollar, sharing 0.25%–0.50% with the corporate client while retaining 1.10%–1.45% net platform margin
metrics: Total annualized Gross Payment Volume (GPV $) converted from ACH/check to Virtual Card (target: 25–45% of total AP)
Net retained interchange spread in basis points (110–145 bps) after bank processor fees and client revenue share
Vendor card-acceptance retention rate (%) across repeat monthly invoices

platform_risks.failure_mode: Vendor card-surcharging pushback or Visa/Mastercard Level-2/Level-3 large-ticket interchange downgrade
platform_risks.trigger: Large vendors refusing card settlement or failing to pass Level-3 line-item tax/invoice metadata with the authorization
platform_risks.impact: Shift of specific vendors back to low-margin ACH or interchange rate step-down
platform_risks.detection_metric: Automated Level-2/Level-3 data-enrichment pass rate and per-vendor surcharge detection
platform_risks.fallback: Automatically inject Level-3 line-item invoice metadata at card creation, offer dynamic early-pay ACH discounts (1.5%–2% 10-day net) for card-averse vendors, and focus on fragmented long-tail vendor bases

plays.name: Whitelisted Agency Ad-Spend Card-Multiplier Points & Volume-Rebate Cycling
plays.mechanism: Route genuine client-authorized advertising spend through eligible agency payment arrangements to earn contract-permitted rewards and volume rebates, net of financing, processing, and client pass-through obligations.
inputs: Client media mandates and rebate ownership clauses
Issuer reward categories, caps, and repayment terms
Platform invoices and agency volume-rebate agreements
workflow: 1. Verify client authorization, platform payment permissions, and ownership of rewards and rebates
2. Model eligible media purchases against reward caps, fees, liquidity, and rebate thresholds
3. Pay only genuine approved advertising invoices without circular spend or fabricated transactions
4. Reconcile settled rewards, client credits, refunds, and full card repayment each statement cycle
metrics: Net retained rewards and rebates per media dollar
Unfunded client exposure and repayment coverage
Invoice-to-reward reconciliation variance

platform_risks.failure_mode: Reward clawback or client-funded liquidity shortfall
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible categories, prohibited payment aggregation, or delayed client reimbursement
platform_risks.impact: Lost rebates, interest costs, and card suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Denied reward value and overdue client balances versus cash reserves
platform_risks.fallback: Move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms and stop rewards-dependent spending

plays.name: Aged Shelf-Corp Reinstatement, Primary Tradeline & 0%-APR Corporate Credit Stacking
plays.mechanism: Compare reinstated entities and genuine business credit facilities for working-capital financing; entity age is not operating history, and promotional APR economics require accurate underwriting and repayment capacity.
inputs: Entity filings, beneficial ownership, and liability searches
Verified operating financials and genuine supplier tradelines
Lender eligibility, promotional APR, fee, and guarantee terms
workflow: 1. Audit the entity's ownership, tax liabilities, and reinstatement requirements
2. Disclose acquisition and actual operating history; establish only genuine paid supplier accounts
3. Compare lender-approved applications with full debt disclosure and consolidated exposure limits
4. Fund documented business expenses and repay before promotional expiry using cash-flow reserves
metrics: Effective borrowing cost including fees
Debt service coverage under post-promotion APR
Utilization and days to promotional expiry

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit withdrawal or unaffordable repricing
platform_risks.trigger: Misstated operating history, undisclosed debt, or expired promotional terms
platform_risks.impact: Account closure, accelerated repayment, and guarantee exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Underwriting discrepancies and stressed repayment coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending

plays.name: High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels
plays.mechanism: Replace blind cold mass-DM blasts (which die to PeerFloodError and silent Message Request graveyards) with high-velocity comment-to-DM triggers, hand-raiser reaction hooks, and multi-inbox warm signal routing.
inputs: Short-form / community trigger posts ('Comment KEYWORD')
Signal-verified prospect handles
Automated DM qualification & booking bridge
workflow: Publish high-curiosity teardown or resource posts where prospects comment a trigger keyword or react to unlock a playbook or calculator
Deliver instant automated DM replies to warm hand-raisers (bypassing cold-DM filters because the user initiated interaction) or send contextual 1-to-1 DMs referencing an active public request
Qualify budget and timeline inside a 3-message DM micro-funnel and transition immediately to a booked call, checkout link, or owned SMS/email list
metrics: Trigger-comment to DM delivery rate
DM reply-to-qualified-conversation %
Revenue per 100 DM threads

platform_risks.failure_mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting
platform_risks.trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts
platform_risks.impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency
platform_risks.fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)
platform_risks.trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox
platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap

plays.name: Programmatic 'Alternative To / Pricing / Cancel' Intent Hijacking
plays.mechanism: Generate programmatic nominative-fair-use comparison matrices, live fee calculators, and migration guides targeting bottom-of-funnel '[Competitor] pricing', '[Competitor] cancel', and '[Competitor] vs [Offer]' queries to intercept buyers with 10–18% conversion rates.
inputs: Competitor pricing tiers, hidden-fee schedules, & cancellation friction data
Bottom-of-funnel '[Brand] pricing / alternative / vs' keyword taxonomy
Interactive side-by-side TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) switching calculator
workflow: Ingest verified public pricing, contract lock-in terms, and fee schedules across 100+ incumbent providers in the target vertical
Publish objective, factual side-by-side comparison matrices and switching calculators under nominative fair use
Offer a 1-click migration concierge or instant savings quote that routes high-intent switchers into owned SaaS, agency, or high-ticket affiliate offers
metrics: Bottom-of-funnel visitor-to-lead conversion % (10–18% target)
Earnings per click (EPC) on switching-intent queries
Organic top-3 SERP share across '[Competitor] pricing/alternative' clusters

platform_risks.failure_mode: UDRP trademark complaint, DMCA notice, or false-advertising cease-and-desist
platform_risks.trigger: Impersonating competitor login pages, using trademarked logos deceptively, or publishing fabricated competitor pricing
platform_risks.impact: Page takedown demand or affiliate partner account review
platform_risks.detection_metric: Quarterly pricing fact-check audit log and legal/compliance inbox alerts
platform_risks.fallback: Rely strictly on nominative fair use (text-only brand names, timestamped public pricing citations, and zero logo spoofing)

plays.name: Telegram Channel & Deal-Room Signal Scraping
plays.mechanism: Ingest public Telegram channel broadcasts, OTC deal rooms, wholesale distress feeds, and niche community message streams in real time to extract high-intent buyer/seller triggers before they hit public search—while avoiding naive member-list scraping traps.
inputs: Public Telegram channel & group broadcast streams
Keyword & entity-regex signal filters
Inbound utility-bot & deal-desk capture endpoints
workflow: Monitor public channel message history and live broadcast streams for high-intent deal keywords (buying, distressed lot, urgent allocation, broker needed)
Score and deduplicate message authors and deal metadata against minimum ticket thresholds without scraping hidden member rosters
Route verified deal signals to an operator desk or deploy a pinned niche utility bot (alert/calculator/directory) that converts channel readers into inbound leads
metrics: Signal-to-response latency (seconds)
Qualified deal triggers per 1,000 messages
Inbound bot opt-in & close rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: MTProto session ban (UserDeactivatedBanError) or FloodWaitError throttling
platform_risks.trigger: Aggressive GetParticipantsRequest calls on hidden member lists or high-frequency polling from VoIP virtual SIMs
platform_risks.impact: Immediate termination of listener sessions and loss of real-time channel feed ingestion
platform_risks.detection_metric: Telegram FloodWaitError seconds per hour and session disconnect rate
platform_risks.fallback: Restrict ingestion to passive read-only public broadcast listeners and capture prospects inbound via official Bot API utility bots

candidates.uncertainty_note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.

automation_levers: Automated export BOL & 8-digit HTS substitution reconciler
B2B antitrust/interchange AP ledger claim packager
key_risks: CBP liquidation deadline or missing export trace defects
regulatory_notes: Execute all formal CBP drawback and protest filings through a licensed 19 CFR Part 111 customs broker or trade counsel under valid Customs Powers of Attorney and 19 CFR Part 190 recordkeeping.
Provide court-required third-party class-action filer disclosures clarifying that claimants may file directly at zero cost.

inputs: Importer authorization, importer-of-record identifiers, ACE entry and liquidation extracts, Form 7501 line detail, duty-payment evidence, and existing drawback or protest histories; commercial manifests supply leads rather than proof of eligibility.

Export bills of lading, AES/ITN records where applicable, inventory and manufacturing records, destruction documentation, transfer certificates, and evidence establishing the claimant's rights without duplicate recovery.

Broker and trade-counsel engagements, provision-specific eligibility and deadline matrix, duty-type exclusions, claimant contingency terms, and an itemized budget for historical-data extraction, evidence reconstruction, and filing.
plays.mechanism: Match ImportGenius/Panjiva shipment leads to importer-authorized ACE entry summaries, CBP Form 7501 data, and export or supervised-destruction evidence; 19 U.S.C. § 1313 generally permits recovery of up to 99% of eligible duties, taxes, and fees, subject to the selected drawback provision's matching, timing, and documentary requirements. Licensed 19 CFR Part 111 customs brokers perform reserved customs business and trade counsel handles legal positions, while the desk separates drawback from § 1514 protests, generally due within 180 days of liquidation or another protestable decision, and excludes antidumping/countervailing duties and other expressly ineligible assessments rather than treating all tariffs as recoverable. Target a 25%–35% contingency only on realized CBP Treasury refunds under contracts permitted for the service provider, with broker/counsel compensation separately structured to avoid prohibited unlicensed customs business or referral-fee sharing and with document reconstruction, filing, and professional costs disclosed separately from gross claims.
metrics: Supported collectible base: eligible paid duties, taxes, and fees multiplied by the applicable recovery percentage, less prior recoveries and unsupported amounts; report manifest-derived opportunities separately.
Cash economics: realized Treasury refunds, contingency receipts at 25%–35%, importer net recovery after disclosed costs, and desk contribution after evidence-acquisition and servicing expense.
Execution quality: percentage of claims with complete entry-to-disposition evidence, days remaining to each statutory deadline, refund realization rate, and post-payment adjustment exposure.
plays.name: Five-Year CBP ACE Duty-Drawback and Tariff-Protest Recovery Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Unsupported claimed dollars divided by proposed claim dollars, duplicate-entry incidence, and unresolved evidence exceptions before filing.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Manifest matching produces an apparently valuable claim that lacks eligible duties, claimant rights, or auditable export/destruction linkage.
platform_risks.fallback: Remove unsupported lines, pursue only independently timely and supportable alternatives through the broker or counsel, and stop reconstruction when expected net recovery no longer covers its cost.
platform_risks.impact: CBP denies or reduces recovery, reconstruction costs become unrecoverable, and paid accelerated drawback may require repayment with additional consequences.
platform_risks.trigger: ACE reconciliation reveals excluded assessments, substitution-rule failures, duplicate claims, missing transfer records, or an expired filing window.

workflow: 1. Obtain importer permission and reconcile manifest leads to paid ACE entries; segregate eligible duty components, potential drawback provisions, § 1514 issues, and entries already refunded, claimed, protested, or outside the relevant deadline.

2. Have the licensed broker and trade counsel validate direct-identification or substitution requirements, export/destruction timing, claimant rights, and required privileges or notices; generally track export/destruction within five years of importation and complete drawback filing within five years of export/destruction, subject to the applicable provision.

3. Build an entry-to-export or destruction evidence ledger, price unresolved documentation gaps, and submit supported claims or timely protests through the authorized professional without using a protest to bypass an expired statutory claim route.

4. Reconcile Treasury receipts, offsets, claim reductions, accelerated-payment exposure, and final liquidation; invoice the agreed percentage only against realized refunds and maintain records and reserves for audit adjustments or repayment.

inputs: Importer-authorized ACE entry-line exports, original classifications and preference claims, liquidation dates, invoices, product specifications, composition and use evidence, and actual duty payments.

Relevant CROSS decisions and their modification or revocation history, HTSUS legal notes and applicable interpretive rules, and USMCA or other FTA certifications supported by production and origin records.

Licensed-broker and trade-counsel engagements, entry-specific PSC/protest/FTA deadline calendar, prior-refund ledger, and quoted costs for technical analysis, origin substantiation, translations, and filing.
plays.mechanism: Audit import lines against the HTSUS, product specifications, CBP CROSS rulings, and agreement-specific origin evidence, recognizing that another importer's published ruling is persuasive only to the extent its facts and legal analysis fit and does not itself bind CBP for this importer. Licensed customs brokers and trade counsel select the available route: an ACE Post-Summary Correction for eligible unliquidated entries, a timely § 1514 protest for protestable liquidation errors, or a qualifying § 1520(d) post-importation preference claim generally filed within one year of importation for an agreement covered by that statute, including USMCA. The collectible base is supported historical overpayment actually refundable through the selected route, net of offsets and professional/documentation costs; prospective landed-cost savings remain a separate forecast and never count as collected refunds.
metrics: Historical recovery funnel: identified overpayment, legally reachable and evidence-supported refund base, accepted adjustments, and realized Treasury receipts after offsets.
Net recovery efficiency: collected refunds less broker, counsel, origin-documentation, and desk charges, with servicing hours and acquisition costs per recovered dollar.
Prospective performance: verified duty-rate change and realized savings on subsequent imports, reported separately from retroactive refunds and from untested volume forecasts.
plays.name: CBP CROSS HTS Reclassification, PSC and FTA Retroactive-Refund Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of proposed refund dollars lacking verified product facts, current legal support, origin substantiation, or a valid filing route.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A superficially similar CROSS ruling or incomplete origin certification supports an invalid refund position.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported positions, preserve independently valid timely claims, retain the supported classification, and obtain additional technical evidence or a prospective binding ruling before changing future treatment.
platform_risks.impact: Refunds are denied, future entries may be underpaid, and the importer incurs amendment, assessment, and professional-review costs.
platform_risks.trigger: Technical review finds materially different product facts, a revoked ruling, unmet origin requirements, or an entry outside the chosen correction or claim window.

workflow: 1. Reconcile paid entry lines to liquidation status and product facts; estimate historical overpayment separately from future import-volume savings and exclude entries with duplicate recovery or no remaining statutory route.

2. Have the broker and counsel test the proposed classification against HTSUS text, legal notes, and factually relevant CROSS rulings; verify agreement-specific origin rules rather than relying on a supplier certificate alone.

3. Submit an eligible PSC generally within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline comes first, a timely § 1514 protest where appropriate, or a complete qualifying § 1520(d) claim within its one-year importation deadline; verify current ACE restrictions and do not substitute one route for another's expired deadline.

4. Reconcile liquidation changes and actual Treasury payments to each entry, deduct agreed recovery costs, and separately implement supported classifications or seek a prospective binding ruling for future entries without counting projected savings as refund cash.

plays.name: CBP "First-Sale Rule" (19 CFR § 152.103) Multi-Tier Customs Valuation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Restructuring multi-tiered import supply chains under the US Court of Appeals *Nissho Iwai* 'First Sale Rule' so US importers legally declare the lower factory-to-middleman transaction price ($8) for US Customs duty and tariff calculation rather than the middleman-to-US-importer invoice price ($18)—slashing annual tariff cash outflows by 35–55% across $10M–$250M+ in imported merchandise.
inputs: US Customs bill-of-lading and HTS duty-spend intelligence identifying mid-market importers paying $1M–$20M/yr in duties via trading companies
Three-party contract, factory cost-sheet, and arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation templates satisfying CBP *Nissho Iwai* criteria
Licensed customs brokerage and trade-attorney opinion pipeline

Audit the two-tier transaction chain to confirm (1) bona fide sale from factory to middleman, (2) clear designation for US export at factory order, and (3) arm's-length pricing
Implement compliant multi-tier invoicing and ERP documentary trails so the customs broker declares the factory's First-Sale price on CBP Form 7501 instead of the middleman's marked-up invoice
Collect a 25–35% contingency fee on all prospective and retroactive (Post-Summary Correction / Protest) duty reductions realized by the importer
metrics: Percentage reduction in declared customs dutiable value (typically 30–50%)
Annualized cash tariff savings ($300k–$5M+/yr per importer) and retroactive PSC refund recovery ($)
CBP CF-28/CF-29 Request for Information audit survival rate (100% documentary compliance)

plays.name: Section 321 "De Minimis" & Border Bonded-Warehouse Tariff Split-Shipping Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Routing bulk sea/air container imports for high-tariff DTC and marketplace brands into Tijuana (IMMEX) or Canadian border-zone bonded 3PL warehouses instead of US ports, then fulfilling individual US consumer orders across the border daily under 19 U.S.C. § 1321 (Section 321 Entry Type 86)—legally eliminating 15%–42.5% customs duties on qualifying consumer parcels and charging brands 35–50% of the saved tariff bill plus 3PL fulfillment fees.
inputs: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) database cross-referenced against US Customs Bill-of-Lading import records (ImportYeti / Panjiva / Datamyne)
Nearshore Mexican IMMEX or Canadian customs-bonded fulfillment center 5–15 miles from San Ysidro/Otay Mesa or Windsor/Blaine border crossings
Automated CBP ACE Entry Type 86 manifest software transmitting 10-digit HTS and consignee data per individual consumer parcel
workflow: Scrape public maritime Bill-of-Lading records to identify US apparel, footwear, luggage, and consumer-goods brands importing 20+ containers/yr in 18%–37.5% HTS duty brackets
Divert the client's ocean containers in-bond (IT/T&E bond) directly to the nearshore border-zone fulfillment facility without paying US bulk entry duties
Sync the warehouse WMS with the brand's Shopify/Amazon store so each US consumer order (<$800 retail value, 1 per person per day) is picked, packed, and cleared via CBP Entry Type 86 at $0 duty
Line-item bill the brand for standard pick-and-pack fulfillment plus a 35–50% contingency split of the verified customs duties eliminated
metrics: Annualized customs duty eliminated ($500k–$10M+/yr per enterprise brand client)
Net tariff-savings share + 3PL margin ($) per parcel cleared across the border
CBP Type 86 automated release rate (>99.4%) and border transit time (<6 hours to USPS/FedEx domestic injection)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory exclusion of specific Section 301 country-of-origin SKUs from Section 321 de minimis eligibility
platform_risks.trigger: Executive/statutory rulemaking removing China-origin Section 301 HTS codes from Entry Type 86 eligibility or tightening 10-digit HTS description rules

inputs: Customer authorization, carrier account access through approved interfaces, invoice line items, tracking events, package dimensions and weights, and payment or credit records.
Effective carrier contracts, tariff versions, negotiated dimensional divisors, minimum-net-charge provisions, service-guarantee exclusions and claim deadlines by service and geography.
Contingency agreement specifying a 35%–50% fee on realized recoveries, treatment of existing customer disputes, and a separate methodology for compensation on negotiated prospective savings.

Recover eligible late-delivery guarantee, dimensional-weight and duplicate-billing overcharges for a negotiated 35%–50% of realized refunds, excluding suspended guarantees, waived rights and expired claims. Separately negotiate minimum-net-charge caps or floors where the carrier offers them, measuring prospective savings against an agreed shipment-level baseline rather than treating a valid contractual minimum as an overcharge.
metrics: Realized refund yield: verified carrier credits or cash received divided by audited parcel spend, segmented by late delivery, dimensional weight and duplicate billing.
Claims acceptance and timeliness: accepted dollars divided by submitted dollars, with the percentage of eligible claims filed before the applicable deadline.

plays.name: Parcel Carrier Late-Delivery, Dim-Weight and Minimum-Net-Charge Recovery Operator

plays.name: Two-Tier Cloud Distributor & Partner-of-Record (CPOR/VIP/CSP) Margin-Split Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Onboard under two-tier cloud distributors Pax8, Ingram Micro Cloud and TD SYNNEX, and Technology Services Distributors Telarus and Avant, to pursue 15%–28% wholesale channel tiers on Adobe VIP Marketplace, Zoom Up / RingCentral UCaaS, Microsoft CSP, Google Workspace and DocuSign. Cold-call SMBs paying retail card rates and execute authorized Reseller-of-Record transfers targeting zero downtime, immediate invoice reductions of 8%–14% and an 8%–15% evergreen annual renewal spread. These are illustrative targets subject to vendor eligibility, compatible discount and spread bases, renewal windows and written distributor terms, not guaranteed margins.
inputs: Approved distributor and master-agent agreements with vendor-specific wholesale tiers, transfer eligibility and renewal residual schedules
Client-authorized subscription invoices, tenant identifiers and renewal dates plus a lawfully sourced SMB calling list and outreach compliance controls
Signed reseller transfer consent, prefunded ACH/card billing mandates and a subscription-level landed-cost and retained-spread ledger
workflow: 1. Complete distributor onboarding and verify each vendor program, partner role, transfer window and written wholesale or residual entitlement.
2. Cold-call eligible SMBs under applicable FTC TSR B2B telemarketing, TCPA and state rules, then compare authorized invoices against verified channel quotes.
3. Obtain client approval and execute the vendor-supported Reseller-of-Record transfer without changing workloads, validating continuity before billing cutover.
4. Reconcile distributor billing and prefunded client collections, measure actual savings and retained spreads and revalidate pricing before each renewal.
metrics: Verified client invoice savings percentage on like-for-like subscription terms
Collected annual renewal spread after distributor costs, support and credit losses
Transfer service-interruption count and prefunded coverage of annual NCE obligations

platform_risks.failure_mode: Partner-tier compression or client default erases the retained spread while annual commitments remain payable
platform_risks.trigger: Vendor rebate changes, ineligible transfer terms or failed client collections on Microsoft NCE annual commitments
platform_risks.impact: Negative contribution, uncollectible subscription balances and potential service interruption
platform_risks.detection_metric: Renewal spread below contracted floor and unfunded noncancelable subscription obligations
platform_risks.fallback: Pause new commitments, enforce agreed prepayment controls and negotiate authorized renewal repricing or vendor-supported transfers without promising cancellation of binding terms

plays.name: Private B2B Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) Umbrella & Contingent Spend-Audit Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Pool 10,000–75,000+ seats and indirect corporate spend across hundreds of SMB member companies under authorized master GPO volume brackets through Una, OMNIA or private vertical SaaS, parcel and telecom GPOs. Pair negotiated brackets with quarter-end vendor price-floor benchmarking informed by Vendr/Tropic playbooks, targeting 3%–12% vendor-paid administrative rebates and 25%–35% contingent Year-1 shared-savings splits under no savings, no fee agreements. Eligibility, rebate bases and benchmark access must be verified; disclose dual compensation and avoid double-counting rebates in client savings.
inputs: Executed GPO member and supplier agreements defining eligible aggregated spend, volume brackets, administrative rebates and compensation disclosures
Member-authorized invoices and seat inventories plus lawfully obtained, like-for-like Vendr/Tropic-style pricing benchmarks
Contingent audit contracts defining the Year-1 savings baseline, exclusions, 25%–35% fee schedule and independent reconciliation rights
workflow: 1. Enroll eligible SMB members with written authority and aggregate verified seat demand and indirect spend without exchanging competitively sensitive data.
2. Validate GPO purchasing eligibility and negotiate supplier volume brackets using lawful quarter-end benchmarks for comparable service and commitment terms.
3. Present disclosed vendor rebates and contingent fees, secure member approval and implement authorized contract changes against an agreed savings baseline.
4. Reconcile actual Year-1 savings and vendor rebates, charge only earned shared-savings fees and audit bracket eligibility and renewal pricing.
metrics: Verified eligible seats and annual member spend within contracted GPO brackets
Realized Year-1 member savings net of contingent fees on a normalized baseline
Collected administrative rebates and shared-savings fees net of reversals

platform_risks.failure_mode: Ineligible pooled spend or disputed savings invalidates rebates and contingent fees
platform_risks.trigger: Supplier audit, volume-bracket shortfall, undisclosed dual compensation or an unsupported baseline adjustment
platform_risks.impact: Rebate clawbacks, member fee disputes and loss of supplier access
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unsupported eligible spend and disputed savings or rebates as a percentage of billed compensation
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend disputed fees, reconcile documented baselines with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts and move affected members to eligible purchasing agreements

plays.name: Multi-Tenant MSP & Distressed Enterprise SaaS Commit Pooling Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Acquire or sub-allocate underutilized multi-year enterprise SaaS/cloud minimums, distressed startup seat blocks and authorized multi-tenant MSP management tiers at a target 35%–65% discount to retail list price only where the vendor explicitly permits assignment or resale. Provision isolated workspaces or managed seats for mid-market clients within applicable Microsoft SPLA/CSP/GDAP, Adobe multi-seat and AWS Marketplace CPPO rules. These programs are not interchangeable: delegated administration alone grants no resale rights, and unused commitments or startup discounts are not presumed transferable.
inputs: Vendor-approved assignment, resale or MSP agreements for identified excess commitments and seat blocks, including distressed-seller authority and title checks
Program-specific entitlement inventory covering Microsoft SPLA/CSP/GDAP, Adobe multi-seat and AWS Marketplace CPPO permissions and end-customer restrictions
Committed client demand, isolated tenant provisioning and a license-audit ledger with prepaid billing and noncancelable commitment reserves
workflow: 1. Verify seller authority and obtain explicit vendor approval for each assignment or sub-allocation before pricing discounted excess capacity.
2. Match committed mid-market demand to permitted SKUs, tenant boundaries and contract terms, stress-testing utilization against unavoidable minimums.
3. Provision isolated workspaces or managed seats through authorized program channels with least-privilege administration and traceable client entitlements.
4. Reconcile seat usage, invoices and license evidence monthly, right-size commitments at permitted windows and remediate audit exceptions promptly.
metrics: Verified acquisition discount to comparable retail list price for approved terms
Collected managed-seat contribution after commitments, support and idle capacity
Entitlement reconciliation exceptions and tenant-isolation control failures

platform_risks.failure_mode: Unauthorized seat pooling or assignment breaches vendor license and tenant-isolation boundaries
platform_risks.trigger: License audit identifies nontransferable distressed seat blocks, unapproved resale or cross-tenant entitlement reuse
platform_risks.impact: License clawbacks, account suspension, stranded commitments and customer data or service exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Provisioned seats lacking vendor-approved entitlement evidence and unresolved tenant-isolation alerts
platform_risks.fallback: Stop unauthorized provisioning, isolate affected access and coordinate vendor-approved direct licenses or permitted migration while resolving audit liabilities transparently

inputs: Weekly HTTP script-tag, DOM header, & DNS TXT/CNAME technographic crawler
Historical install-timestamp ledger (calculating 12-month contract renewal windows)
B2B executive contact graph & migration-agency/SaaS partner routing
workflow: Scan 500,000+ target B2B domains weekly for JavaScript SDKs, tracking pixels, and SPF/CNAME records of $20k–$150k/yr SaaS platforms
Flag accounts entering Month 10 of their annual contract (60 days before auto-renewal lock-in) or accounts running dual competing tags during a live evaluation
Route renewal-window and active-churn signals to competing SaaS sales teams, software resellers, and implementation agencies
metrics: Install/drop detection precision (%) and renewal-date accuracy
Outbound reply-to-demo conversion rate on Month-10 renewal targets
Per-opportunity bounty or retainer revenue per agency/SaaS partner

plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms

Partnerperk/incubator affiliation tiers (Y Combinator Startup School, Stripe Atlas, Mercury Raise, Microsoft for Startups)
Multi-provider LLM and cloud workload router abstracting inference across AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and GCP Vertex
workflow: Provision dedicated vertical micro-SaaS products with live billing, production authentication, and verified corporate domains
Enroll each entity in legitimate startup credit programs to secure $25k–$350k in non-dilutive compute, GPU, and LLM token grants
Route high-volume B2B document parsing, skip-tracing, programmatic content generation, or audio/video transcription workloads across active grant balances

Sell the resulting B2B intelligence, API access, or SaaS subscriptions for hard cash while tracking credit burn and migrating matured workloads to reserved or open-weight self-hosted inference before grant expiration

inputs: BaaS / Commercial Card Issuing bank partnership (Marqeta, Lithic, Stripe Issuing, Highnote, Cross River) on uncapped Visa/Mastercard Large-Ticket & Purchasing interchange tiers
ERP/accounting connector (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, McLeod/TMW freight TMS) ingesting open vendor AP ledgers
Automated vendor-enablement call/email engine pitching 'Day-1 Instant Payment via Virtual Card vs. Net-45 Check/ACH'
workflow: Onboard mid-market companies with $20M–$250M/yr in fragmented vendor payables onto a $0-cost AP automation and working-capital portal
Cross-reference their vendor master list against Visa/Mastercard supplier-acceptance networks to flag vendors that already accept card payments
Offer remaining vendors immediate Day-1 invoice settlement via single-use emailed/API virtual card in exchange for waiving Net-30/Net-60 wait times
Earn 1.50%–1.95% gross interchange rebate from the issuing bank on every settled dollar, sharing 0.25%–0.50% with the corporate client while retaining 1.10%–1.45% net platform margin
metrics: Total annualized Gross Payment Volume (GPV $) converted from ACH/check to Virtual Card (target: 25–45% of total AP)
Net retained interchange spread in basis points (110–145 bps) after bank processor fees and client revenue share
Vendor card-acceptance retention rate (%) across repeat monthly invoices

key_risks: Slow municipal or utility refund issuance
regulatory_notes: Observe Treasury Circular 230 §10.27 contingent-fee rules on federal tax returns, state property-tax consultant licensing, and carrier API terms.
Secure signed Letters of Authorization and baseline invoice snapshots before disclosing tariff or refund findings.

inputs: Customer authorization, carrier account access through approved interfaces, invoice line items, tracking events, package dimensions and weights, and payment or credit records.
Effective carrier contracts, tariff versions, negotiated dimensional divisors, minimum-net-charge provisions, service-guarantee exclusions and claim deadlines by service and geography.
Contingency agreement specifying a 35%–50% fee on realized recoveries, treatment of existing customer disputes, and a separate methodology for compensation on negotiated prospective savings.
plays.mechanism: Audit authorized FedEx Billing Online, UPS Billing Center and DHL invoice exports against shipment events, measured dimensions and the customer's effective service agreements. Recover eligible late-delivery guarantee, dimensional-weight and duplicate-billing overcharges for a negotiated 35%–50% of realized refunds, excluding suspended guarantees, waived rights and expired claims. Separately negotiate minimum-net-charge caps or floors where the carrier offers them, measuring prospective savings against an agreed shipment-level baseline rather than treating a valid contractual minimum as an overcharge.
metrics: Realized refund yield: verified carrier credits or cash received divided by audited parcel spend, segmented by late delivery, dimensional weight and duplicate billing.
Claims acceptance and timeliness: accepted dollars divided by submitted dollars, with the percentage of eligible claims filed before the applicable deadline.
Operator contribution: collected contingency fees minus data, submission and dispute costs; report prospective minimum-charge savings separately from refunds.
plays.name: Parcel Carrier Late-Delivery, Dim-Weight and Minimum-Net-Charge Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Weekly rejection dollars by reason, missed-deadline count, authentication failures and credit-posting latency relative to the carrier-specific baseline.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The carrier rejects claims or restricts access because guarantee eligibility, filing rules or supported integration methods differ from the audit assumptions.
platform_risks.fallback: Pause the affected automation, use authorized exports and supported manual submission channels, and restrict recovery forecasts to confirmed eligible services and open filing windows.
platform_risks.impact: Expected recoveries disappear, processing costs rise and unsupported automation can jeopardize customer account access.
platform_risks.trigger: A guarantee suspension, contractual waiver, claim-window change, undocumented endpoint dependency or portal authentication change.

workflow: 1. Import customer-authorized exports or documented APIs, normalize tracking and invoice identifiers, and create a deadline queue without assuming every carrier provides a claims-submission API.

2. Recalculate eligible charges and delivery commitments using the applicable contract version; remove guarantee suspensions, customer-caused exceptions, duplicates already credited and claims outside their filing window.
3. Submit evidence-backed claims through permitted carrier channels, track acknowledgments and appeals, and present minimum-net-charge negotiation scenarios separately from historical billing errors.
4. Reconcile posted credits to invoices and customer receipts, invoice the agreed contingency only on realized recovery, and monitor negotiated pricing against the agreed baseline.

inputs: Up to 36 months of utility bills, interval-demand data, meter maps, cooling-tower water balances or approved submeters, waste invoices, commercial leases and CAM reconciliations.
Effective utility tariffs, demand-ratchet schedules, sewer-credit rules, manufacturing exemption requirements, waste escalation terms, CAM exclusions and contractual audit deadlines.

Customer authorization and a recovery agreement specifying refund contingencies, prospective shared-savings duration, weather and occupancy adjustments, and supporting engineering or tax-specialist responsibilities.
plays.mechanism: Review up to 36 months of commercial electric, water/sewer, waste and lease CAM charges, subject to each tariff's, contract's and jurisdiction's recovery limits. Test demand-ratchet application, cooling-tower evaporation sewer credits, qualifying manufacturing-meter tax exemptions, waste-hauler escalation clauses and lease-specific CAM allocations against documented eligibility. Charge a negotiated 35%–50% of realized refunds and a separately defined share of verified prospective savings, avoiding double charging the same benefit.
metrics: Realized recovery by category and site: collected refunds or usable credits divided by audited utility, waste and CAM spend.
Verified recurring savings: adjusted baseline charges minus actual post-change charges, controlling for tariff movements, usage, weather, occupancy and service scope.
Recovery efficiency: investigation cost per recovered dollar, median days to credit and percentage of claimed amounts supported by accepted documentation.
plays.name: Commercial Utility, Waste and CAM Historical Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of proposed recovery dollars lacking required evidence, denial rate by rule and incidence of post-adjustment reversals.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A utility, hauler or landlord denies recovery because the claimed classification or credit lacks contemporaneous eligibility evidence.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported items, pursue documented disputes within surviving deadlines, and implement properly documented prospective metering or classification changes where economically justified.
platform_risks.impact: Historical refunds are reduced or eliminated, and an unsupported prospective adjustment can generate later rebilling.
platform_risks.trigger: Missing cooling-tower metering, an expired lease audit period, unavailable historical tariffs or a manufacturing exemption that does not apply to the billed meter.

workflow: 1. Build a site-and-meter ledger covering the requested 36-month period, identify shorter recovery windows, and preserve timely utility disputes and lease audit notices.

2. Recalculate demand ratchets, eligible evaporation deductions, qualifying manufacturing exemptions, waste increases and CAM allocations using actual tariff and lease provisions rather than assumed universal credits.

3. Submit supported correction requests to utilities, haulers and landlords; obtain required meter verification or exemption documentation and distinguish refundable errors from prospective tariff changes.
4. Reconcile cash refunds and posted credits, establish adjusted post-change baselines, and invoice the 35%–50% recovery fee plus any non-overlapping, contractually defined shared savings.

Member-authorized invoices and seat inventories plus lawfully obtained, like-for-like Vendr/Tropic-style pricing benchmarks

Realized Year-1 member savings net of contingent fees on a normalized baseline

automation_levers: 835 ERA RARC/CARC underpayment & ERISA plan classifier
FAIR Health / clinical-acuity baseball-arbitration brief builder
key_risks: Forfeited certified-IDR-entity fees on ineligible/state-regulated claims
Delayed payer remittance after prevailing IDR awards
regulatory_notes: Execute HIPAA Business Associate Agreements, screen federal ERISA vs state surprise-billing jurisdiction pre-filing, and comply with 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 / 45 CFR § 149.510 batching and cooling-off rules.
Calculate contingency fees strictly on incremental cash collected above the payer initial QPA payment net of unrecovered IDR fees.

inputs: Provider-authorized 835 ERA and 837 claim data, initial-payment or denial receipt dates, payer explanations, QPA disclosures, service codes, facility status, network status, and patient cost-sharing allocations under appropriate privacy and security agreements.

Plan funding and ERISA information, applicable state payment-dispute rules, emergency or nonemergency NSA eligibility facts, notice-and-consent records where relevant, and existing negotiation, IDR, or settlement histories.

Authorized-representative and counsel arrangements, current CMS procedures and certified-entity fee schedules, permissible batching criteria, negotiation/filing calendar, and a collection-based contingency agreement defining QPA and initial-payment treatment.
plays.mechanism: Ingest commercial out-of-network 835 ERA remittances for emergency, anesthesia, radiology, and eligible specialty surgical services, then screen federal No Surprises Act eligibility under 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 and related provider provisions against specified state-law or All-Payer Model rules; ERISA status is relevant but does not alone resolve jurisdiction. An authorized representative, with counsel where legal representation requires it, starts open negotiation within the applicable 30-business-day initiation window, completes the 30-business-day negotiation period, and initiates federal IDR within four business days afterward, batching only disputes that satisfy then-current federal criteria through a certified IDR entity. Charge 20%–30% only on incremental payer cash collected above the contractual QPA floor after nonreimbursed federal administrative and certified-entity fees, also excluding the initial payer payment from new recovery because QPA is a statutory benchmark rather than necessarily the initial payment; track evidence preparation and professional costs separately from submitted offers and awards.
metrics: Collectible dispute base: federally eligible disputed dollars with timely negotiation and IDR rights, separated from billed charges, requested offers, and unpaid awards.

Realized economics: incremental cash above both the initial-payment baseline and contractual QPA floor, net unreimbursed process fees, 20%–30% contingency receipts, and contribution after evidence and representative costs.
Process performance: timely initiation rate, eligible-batch acceptance rate, cost per resolved claim, days from determination to payment, and unpaid-award aging.
plays.name: Federal No Surprises Act Open-Negotiation and Certified-IDR Recovery Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Eligibility rejection rate, batch-separation rate, missed-deadline count, and nonreimbursed process cost as a percentage of incremental collections.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Jurisdiction, batching, or timing defects make an apparently profitable federal IDR submission ineligible.
platform_risks.fallback: Separate disputes only where still timely and permitted, use the applicable state process when available, continue permissible payer negotiation, and cease fee-generating submissions with negative expected net recovery.
platform_risks.impact: Disputes are dismissed or delayed, administrative and preparation expenses are stranded, and an award forecast never becomes incremental provider cash.
platform_risks.trigger: State-law review displaces federal IDR, services fail NSA eligibility, a batch violates current criteria, or negotiation and initiation timestamps miss applicable business-day deadlines.

workflow: 1. Reconcile each ERA to its underlying claim and initial-payment or denial receipt date; exclude ineligible services, route disputes governed by applicable state processes appropriately, and verify federal jurisdiction without assuming every ERISA or specialty-surgery claim qualifies.

2. Send the required open-negotiation notice within 30 business days after receipt of initial payment or denial, run the 30-business-day negotiation period, and assemble permissible evidence without using billed charges or prohibited public-payer comparisons.

3. Initiate federal IDR within four business days after negotiation ends, subject to applicable exceptions or extensions; form only currently permissible batches, select a certified entity, and meet offer, fee, and evidence deadlines rather than treating the initiation window as blanket batching authority.

4. Track settlements, determinations, payer payment deadlines, and actual deposits; calculate the fee base as max(0, cumulative comparable payer cash minus max(initial payer payment, contract-defined comparable QPA floor) minus nonreimbursed administrative and certified-entity fees), excluding patient collections and invoicing only after cash arrives.

inputs: Public Form 5500 filings and available Schedule A/C records, employer size and plan-year information, employer-confirmed renewal dates and appropriately obtained business contact details.

Employer authorization, incumbent fee disclosures, plan documents, aggregate claims and pharmacy reports, stop-loss terms, underwriting requirements and privacy-controlled access to necessary participant information.

Licensed broker and specialist relationships, TPA and stop-loss proposals, captive participation terms, PBM rebate and spread definitions, NADAC availability and fallback pricing rules, and a $40–$65 PEPM service proposal.
plays.mechanism: Use public Form 5500 Schedule A/C information, where filed and informative, to identify mid-market renewal and compensation-review opportunities, then offer an employer-authorized CAA 2021 service-provider fee-disclosure review. A properly licensed advisory team can seek broker-of-record appointments and compare bundled coverage with separately contracted TPA, stop-loss or suitable captive arrangements and a transparent pass-through PBM using an explicitly defined NADAC-based pricing methodology. Negotiate recurring $40–$65 PEPM advisory fees where supported by scope and client agreement, with all commissions and indirect compensation disclosed and no assumption that unbundling guarantees savings.
metrics: Recurring advisory revenue: enrolled employees multiplied by the contracted $40–$65 PEPM fee, less servicing costs and disclosed fee offsets.
Risk-adjusted employer cost: claims, administration, stop-loss premiums, pharmacy costs, collateral and runout obligations minus realized rebates and recoveries.
Service and retention quality: renewal retention, disclosure completeness, pharmacy guarantee reconciliation variance and unresolved participant access issues.

3. Compare fully insured and level-funded options using expected and adverse claims scenarios, stop-loss exclusions and lasers, captive collateral, TPA fees, pharmacy guarantees and rebates actually retained by the employer.

4. Implement the employer-selected structure with licensed parties, privacy safeguards and continuity planning; collect agreed PEPM fees and review total costs, disclosures and service performance at each renewal.
