regulatory_notes: Verify state commercial-purpose lending exemptions, usury ceilings and escrow licensing rules.
Release funds strictly to bonded title/settlement agents after verifying unconditional end-buyer cash on deposit.

plays.name: 24-to-72-Hour Escrow-Locked Transactional ("Flash") Double-Close Funding
plays.mechanism: Fund the A->B acquisition only after the title agent independently verifies cleared, unconditional end-buyer B->C funds in escrow and an enforceable closing waterfall. Target a 1.0%–2.5% earned funding fee per 1–3 day turn; closing delays, fraud and legal restrictions can impair returns or principal.
inputs: Executed A->B and B->C purchase contracts, title commitment and independently verified settlement-agent credentials
Cleared end-buyer escrow funds, written disbursement conditions and a reconciled same-transaction payoff waterfall
Commercial-purpose funding agreement reviewed for applicable licensing, usury and escrow requirements
workflow: 1. Underwrite both contracts, title exceptions, end-buyer closing conditions and the settlement agent's authority and applicable bonding or insurance.
2. Independently confirm end-buyer cleared funds and irrevocable disbursement instructions using a previously verified title-agent contact channel.
3. Wire A->B funding only to approved title escrow after all release conditions are satisfied and the closing sequence is documented.
4. Reconcile B->C settlement, recover principal and earned fees, and release capital for reuse only after cleared repayment is confirmed.
metrics: Earned funding fees as a percentage of funded principal per completed turn
Median and maximum hours from funding disbursement to cleared repayment
Unrecovered principal and delayed-closing exposure as a percentage of outstanding funding

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fraudulent wire instructions or conditional end-buyer funds leave the A->B advance unrepaid
platform_risks.trigger: Last-minute beneficiary changes, failed independent callbacks or unresolved B->C release conditions
platform_risks.impact: Loss of principal, prolonged escrow disputes and interruption of capital recycling
platform_risks.detection_metric: Count of unresolved wire-verification exceptions and funded closings past contractual repayment deadlines
platform_risks.fallback: Stop disbursement, independently reverify settlement instructions and obtain counsel-directed escrow recovery before further funding

plays.name: Earnest-Money Deposit ("Gator") Escrow Lending & Joint-Venture Splits
plays.mechanism: Advance $2,500–$25,000 refundable-contingency earnest-money deposits directly to title escrow under documented JV or promissory protections, with security recorded or perfected where legally appropriate. Negotiate a 15%–30% share of an earned assignment fee or a lawful fixed return; refunds depend on contractual deadlines, valid contingency exercise and escrow release terms.
inputs: Assignable purchase agreement with explicit refundable contingencies, notice procedures and deadline calendar
Verified title escrow account and executed JV or promissory documents with legally appropriate recorded or perfected protections
Borrower diligence, assignment economics and state-specific lending, brokerage, securities and usury review
workflow: 1. Verify assignment rights, counterparty identity, refundable contingencies and the enforceability of the proposed JV or lending structure.
2. Execute repayment and profit-split documents, perfect any lawful security and transmit the deposit directly to verified title escrow.
3. Track contingency and assignment deadlines, require documented progress and deliver timely cancellation notices when authorized and necessary.
4. Reconcile the closing or refund statement, recover deposited principal and collect only the contractually earned fee or lawful return.
metrics: Earned assignment-fee share or fixed return per completed deposit advance
Percentage of active deposits with verified unexpired refund rights and complete documentation
Deposit loss rate and median days from advance to cleared repayment

platform_risks.failure_mode: A supposedly refundable deposit becomes nonrefundable or disputed
platform_risks.trigger: Missed contingency notice deadline, invalid cancellation or unauthorized contract amendment
platform_risks.impact: Deposit forfeiture, delayed recovery and disputes over assignment proceeds
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deposits approaching contingency expiry without documented assignment or cancellation instructions
platform_risks.fallback: Freeze additional advances, seek timely authorized cancellation and pursue counsel-reviewed escrow release or contractual remedies

plays.name: Aged Shelf-Corp Reinstatement, Primary Tradeline & 0%-APR Corporate Credit Stacking
plays.mechanism: Compare reinstated entities and genuine business credit facilities for working-capital financing; entity age is not operating history, and promotional APR economics require accurate underwriting and repayment capacity.
inputs: Entity filings, beneficial ownership, and liability searches
Verified operating financials and genuine supplier tradelines
Lender eligibility, promotional APR, fee, and guarantee terms
workflow: 1. Audit the entity's ownership, tax liabilities, and reinstatement requirements
2. Disclose acquisition and actual operating history; establish only genuine paid supplier accounts
3. Compare lender-approved applications with full debt disclosure and consolidated exposure limits
4. Fund documented business expenses and repay before promotional expiry using cash-flow reserves
metrics: Effective borrowing cost including fees
Debt service coverage under post-promotion APR
Utilization and days to promotional expiry

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit withdrawal or unaffordable repricing
platform_risks.trigger: Misstated operating history, undisclosed debt, or expired promotional terms
platform_risks.impact: Account closure, accelerated repayment, and guarantee exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Underwriting discrepancies and stressed repayment coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending

plays.name: B2B Commercial Virtual Card (VCC) Interchange & AP Settlement Rebate Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Embedding a 'Free Automated Accounts Payable (AP) / Instant Vendor Settlement' platform inside high-volume B2B verticals (freight brokerage, construction general contracting, medical supply, property management, media agencies) that converts checks and ACH payables into single-use Visa/Mastercard Commercial Virtual Credit Cards (VCCs)—capturing 140–195 basis points (1.40%–1.95%) in uncapped commercial interchange rebates on hundreds of millions in third-party invoice volume.
inputs: BaaS / Commercial Card Issuing bank partnership (Marqeta, Lithic, Stripe Issuing, Highnote, Cross River) on uncapped Visa/Mastercard Large-Ticket & Purchasing interchange tiers
ERP/accounting connector (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, McLeod/TMW freight TMS) ingesting open vendor AP ledgers
Automated vendor-enablement call/email engine pitching 'Day-1 Instant Payment via Virtual Card vs. Net-45 Check/ACH'
workflow: Onboard mid-market companies with $20M–$250M/yr in fragmented vendor payables onto a $0-cost AP automation and working-capital portal
Cross-reference their vendor master list against Visa/Mastercard supplier-acceptance networks to flag vendors that already accept card payments
Offer remaining vendors immediate Day-1 invoice settlement via single-use emailed/API virtual card in exchange for waiving Net-30/Net-60 wait times
Earn 1.50%–1.95% gross interchange rebate from the issuing bank on every settled dollar, sharing 0.25%–0.50% with the corporate client while retaining 1.10%–1.45% net platform margin
metrics: Total annualized Gross Payment Volume (GPV $) converted from ACH/check to Virtual Card (target: 25–45% of total AP)
Net retained interchange spread in basis points (110–145 bps) after bank processor fees and client revenue share
Vendor card-acceptance retention rate (%) across repeat monthly invoices

regulatory_notes: Hold active state Life & Health and Property & Casualty producer licenses and deliver full ERISA §408(b)(2) / CAA 2021 compensation disclosures.
Structure stop-loss specific/aggregate attachment points, run-out coverage, and RBP balance-bill legal defense cleanly.

inputs: Public Form 5500 filings and available Schedule A/C records, employer size and plan-year information, employer-confirmed renewal dates and appropriately obtained business contact details.

Employer authorization, incumbent fee disclosures, plan documents, aggregate claims and pharmacy reports, stop-loss terms, underwriting requirements and privacy-controlled access to necessary participant information.

Licensed broker and specialist relationships, TPA and stop-loss proposals, captive participation terms, PBM rebate and spread definitions, NADAC availability and fallback pricing rules, and a $40–$65 PEPM service proposal.
plays.mechanism: Use public Form 5500 Schedule A/C information, where filed and informative, to identify mid-market renewal and compensation-review opportunities, then offer an employer-authorized CAA 2021 service-provider fee-disclosure review. A properly licensed advisory team can seek broker-of-record appointments and compare bundled coverage with separately contracted TPA, stop-loss or suitable captive arrangements and a transparent pass-through PBM using an explicitly defined NADAC-based pricing methodology. Negotiate recurring $40–$65 PEPM advisory fees where supported by scope and client agreement, with all commissions and indirect compensation disclosed and no assumption that unbundling guarantees savings.
metrics: Recurring advisory revenue: enrolled employees multiplied by the contracted $40–$65 PEPM fee, less servicing costs and disclosed fee offsets.
Risk-adjusted employer cost: claims, administration, stop-loss premiums, pharmacy costs, collateral and runout obligations minus realized rebates and recoveries.
Service and retention quality: renewal retention, disclosure completeness, pharmacy guarantee reconciliation variance and unresolved participant access issues.
plays.name: Mid-Market Level-Funded Benefits and Transparent PBM Advisory Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Adverse-scenario funding gap, claims-to-budget variance, unrecovered stop-loss balances and unexplained differences between disclosed and received compensation.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The proposed unbundled plan produces adverse claims exposure or undisclosed compensation despite appearing cheaper on headline premiums.
platform_risks.fallback: Retain or competitively rebid the existing structure when risk-adjusted economics are unfavorable, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks and narrow the engagement to disclosed advisory work until implementation conditions are satisfied.
platform_risks.impact: Employer costs exceed projections, coverage continuity deteriorates and advisory fees or the BOR relationship become disputed.
platform_risks.trigger: Incomplete claims data, stop-loss lasers or exclusions, nonrefundable captive collateral, ambiguous PBM rebate definitions or unsupported NADAC pricing for uncovered products.

workflow: 1. Analyze publicly available filings through permitted access methods, identify likely renewal opportunities and confirm current plan arrangements directly because filings are historical and may omit relevant compensation details.
2. Obtain employer authorization, review applicable CAA 2021 disclosures and existing termination terms, and define advisory deliverables and compensation before requesting any BOR appointment.

3. Compare fully insured and level-funded options using expected and adverse claims scenarios, stop-loss exclusions and lasers, captive collateral, TPA fees, pharmacy guarantees and rebates actually retained by the employer.

4. Implement the employer-selected structure with licensed parties, privacy safeguards and continuity planning; collect agreed PEPM fees and review total costs, disclosures and service performance at each renewal.

inputs: Customer authorization, three to four years of policies and premium audits, payroll registers, job-duty evidence, overtime breakdowns, officer election documents and subcontractor coverage records.
Applicable state classification rules, NCCI or independent-bureau worksheets, experience-period and valuation dates, carrier loss runs and documented claim corrections.
Carrier and bureau dispute procedures, policy-specific correction deadlines, a 30%–40% realized-refund agreement and licensed brokerage support for any BOR renewal engagement.
plays.mechanism: Audit three to four historical policy years where carrier, state and rating-bureau correction rules permit, checking actual duties, payroll classifications, eligible overtime adjustments and officer exclusions or limits. Reconcile NCCI experience-rating worksheets, or the applicable independent bureau's equivalent, to accurate carrier loss reports and valuation dates; an open reserve is not an error merely because the ultimate claim later costs less. Recover documented premium overpayments for a negotiated 30%–40% contingency and pursue separately authorized, properly licensed BOR renewal work.
metrics: Realized premium recovery: received refunds and usable policy credits divided by audited historical premium, segmented by payroll, classification and experience-mod correction.
Correction conversion: dollars recovered divided by dollars submitted, alongside days from supported dispute to revised audit or bureau worksheet.
Renewal economics: separately disclosed brokerage revenue and verified prospective premium effect, controlling for payroll, operations, rates and coverage changes.
plays.name: Workers' Compensation Classification and Experience-Mod Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Rejected correction dollars by reason, percentage of payroll supported by contemporaneous records and net premium change after the full audit.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A carrier or rating bureau rejects proposed corrections because classifications, loss valuations or retroactive deadlines were misinterpreted.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported claims, disclose any additional premium exposure, use the bureau's documented dispute process for defensible items and improve prospective payroll and claims reporting.
platform_risks.impact: No refund is issued, advisory effort is unrecovered and a broader audit may identify additional premium owed.
platform_risks.trigger: Unsupported separation of payroll, missing officer elections, treatment of later reserve reductions as historical errors or submission outside the permitted correction period.

workflow: 1. Map each policy to its governing state and bureau rules, establish the allowable correction window and reconcile audited payroll to contemporaneous employment and job-duty records.
2. Test class-code assignments, permitted overtime premium exclusions, officer elections or payroll limits and subcontractor treatment without relabeling work merely to obtain a cheaper rate.
3. Reconcile experience-mod inputs against losses reported for the applicable valuation date; submit evidenced payroll, classification or loss-data corrections to the carrier and bureau as required.
4. Obtain revised audits or rating worksheets, trace resulting premium credits through endorsements and receipts, collect the 30%–40% contingency and separately quote licensed BOR renewal services.

automation_levers: 55-day statement float, T-bill sweep & ACH ledger
key_risks: Card issuer financial review or shutdown
regulatory_notes: Maintain valid state sales-tax resale certificates, accurate 1099-K / IRC price-adjustment cost-basis records, and strict separation from prohibited consumer card-cycling.
Diversify across vetted Net-3/Net-5 buying groups, insure high-value electronics shipments, and match statement closing cycles to cleared ACH settlements.

inputs: Verified buying-group identity and operating terms, written purchase orders with fixed SKUs and acceptance criteria, warehouse instructions, settlement obligations and return or rejection allocation.

Commercial card agreements showing authorized use, purchase limits, eligible reward rates and caps, bonus conditions, statement timing, actual payment deadlines and any restrictions on resale purchases.

Supplier availability and invoices, documented resale or exemption eligibility where applicable, shipment insurance and tracking, working-capital reserves and a transaction-level inventory and cash ledger.
plays.mechanism: Fulfill genuine, pre-committed buying-group purchase orders through BuyForMeRetail, Pointsmaker or independently verified counterparties, using authorized commercial card purchases and documented delivery to designated warehouses in Delaware, New Hampshire or Oregon. Earn the contracted merchandise spread plus only eligible 2%–4% cashback or bonus value, using uncapped rewards solely when current issuer terms explicitly provide them; tax treatment depends on sourcing, possession, resale documentation and downstream obligations rather than a tax-free warehouse label. Match a contractually verified Net-3 ACH settlement to the actual card due date, which may provide up to approximately 60 days only on suitable products and purchase dates, without circular purchases, fictitious sales or issuer-limit evasion.
metrics: Realized order contribution: buyer proceeds plus posted eligible rewards minus merchandise, freight, tax, insurance, financing, returns and dispute costs.
Cash-conversion spread: actual card payment due date minus cleared buyer settlement date, with stress tests for late acceptance and ACH reversals.
Exposure control: unsettled counterparty receivables, rejected-unit rate and liquid reserves divided by card obligations due before stressed settlement.
plays.name: Pre-Committed Buying-Group Fulfillment and Commercial Card Working-Capital Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Receivables aging beyond the contractual Net-3 start event, rejected deliveries, reward clawbacks and stressed cash coverage below the operator's minimum.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Buying-group acceptance or settlement fails while the card issuer still requires full repayment or reverses expected rewards.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop new purchases, meet card obligations from reserved cash, recover or resell legitimately owned goods through permitted channels and resume only after settlement reliability and issuer eligibility are confirmed.
platform_risks.impact: A nominally profitable order becomes illiquid inventory and unsecured receivables, with interest charges, lost rewards or restricted card access.
platform_risks.trigger: Counterparty insolvency, SKU rejection, warehouse delivery disputes, delayed ACH, reward exclusions or issuer restrictions on purchase and repayment patterns.

workflow: 1. Verify the counterparty and current BuyForMeRetail or Pointsmaker program terms before funding any order; confirm that the PO is genuinely committed rather than treating an indicative buying list as guaranteed demand.

2. Calculate landed margin after tax, shipping, reward exclusions, returns and financing costs; size purchases to available cash repayment capacity and issuer-approved limits rather than assuming all cards provide uncapped rewards or 60-day float.

3. Purchase approved merchandise and ship to the specifically authorized DE, NH or OR warehouse with chain-of-custody evidence, recording title transfer, acceptance events and the exact event that starts Net-3 settlement.

4. Reconcile accepted units and cleared ACH proceeds, reserve for returns or reversals, pay the statement by its actual due date and fund subsequent genuine orders only within verified counterparty and issuer limits.

Enroll each entity in legitimate startup credit programs to secure $25k–$350k in non-dilutive compute, GPU, and LLM token grants

plays.name: B2B Commercial Virtual Card (VCC) Interchange & AP Settlement Rebate Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Embedding a 'Free Automated Accounts Payable (AP) / Instant Vendor Settlement' platform inside high-volume B2B verticals (freight brokerage, construction general contracting, medical supply, property management, media agencies) that converts checks and ACH payables into single-use Visa/Mastercard Commercial Virtual Credit Cards (VCCs)—capturing 140–195 basis points (1.40%–1.95%) in uncapped commercial interchange rebates on hundreds of millions in third-party invoice volume.
inputs: BaaS / Commercial Card Issuing bank partnership (Marqeta, Lithic, Stripe Issuing, Highnote, Cross River) on uncapped Visa/Mastercard Large-Ticket & Purchasing interchange tiers
ERP/accounting connector (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, McLeod/TMW freight TMS) ingesting open vendor AP ledgers
Automated vendor-enablement call/email engine pitching 'Day-1 Instant Payment via Virtual Card vs. Net-45 Check/ACH'
workflow: Onboard mid-market companies with $20M–$250M/yr in fragmented vendor payables onto a $0-cost AP automation and working-capital portal
Cross-reference their vendor master list against Visa/Mastercard supplier-acceptance networks to flag vendors that already accept card payments
Offer remaining vendors immediate Day-1 invoice settlement via single-use emailed/API virtual card in exchange for waiving Net-30/Net-60 wait times
Earn 1.50%–1.95% gross interchange rebate from the issuing bank on every settled dollar, sharing 0.25%–0.50% with the corporate client while retaining 1.10%–1.45% net platform margin

Net retained interchange spread in basis points (110–145 bps) after bank processor fees and client revenue share
Vendor card-acceptance retention rate (%) across repeat monthly invoices

Purchase the sealed master cases via a foreign trading entity, conduct third-party SGS lot authentication, and remove secondary distributor tracking labels that could identify the source distributor
Import the goods legally under First-Sale exhaustion and flip on back-to-back POs to US off-price retail chains, pharmacy wholesalers, and verified marketplace aggregators

100% lot-level manufacturer authenticity verification and chain-of-custody pass rate

Qualified deal triggers per 1,000 messages

plays.name: Section 321 "De Minimis" & Border Bonded-Warehouse Tariff Split-Shipping Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Routing bulk sea/air container imports for high-tariff DTC and marketplace brands into Tijuana (IMMEX) or Canadian border-zone bonded 3PL warehouses instead of US ports, then fulfilling individual US consumer orders across the border daily under 19 U.S.C. § 1321 (Section 321 Entry Type 86)—legally eliminating 15%–42.5% customs duties on qualifying consumer parcels and charging brands 35–50% of the saved tariff bill plus 3PL fulfillment fees.
inputs: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) database cross-referenced against US Customs Bill-of-Lading import records (ImportYeti / Panjiva / Datamyne)
Nearshore Mexican IMMEX or Canadian customs-bonded fulfillment center 5–15 miles from San Ysidro/Otay Mesa or Windsor/Blaine border crossings
Automated CBP ACE Entry Type 86 manifest software transmitting 10-digit HTS and consignee data per individual consumer parcel
workflow: Scrape public maritime Bill-of-Lading records to identify US apparel, footwear, luggage, and consumer-goods brands importing 20+ containers/yr in 18%–37.5% HTS duty brackets
Divert the client's ocean containers in-bond (IT/T&E bond) directly to the nearshore border-zone fulfillment facility without paying US bulk entry duties
Sync the warehouse WMS with the brand's Shopify/Amazon store so each US consumer order (<$800 retail value, 1 per person per day) is picked, packed, and cleared via CBP Entry Type 86 at $0 duty
Line-item bill the brand for standard pick-and-pack fulfillment plus a 35–50% contingency split of the verified customs duties eliminated
metrics: Annualized customs duty eliminated ($500k–$10M+/yr per enterprise brand client)
Net tariff-savings share + 3PL margin ($) per parcel cleared across the border
CBP Type 86 automated release rate (>99.4%) and border transit time (<6 hours to USPS/FedEx domestic injection)

platform_risks.trigger: Executive/statutory rulemaking removing China-origin Section 301 HTS codes from Entry Type 86 eligibility or tightening 10-digit HTS description rules
platform_risks.impact: Loss of Section 321 duty exemption on affected country-of-origin SKUs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time HTS + Country-of-Origin eligibility screen in the WMS before container booking
platform_risks.fallback: Focus on non-301 origin goods (Vietnam, India, EU, Bangladesh, Cambodia) where high MFN duties (16%–32% on apparel/footwear/textiles) remain 100% Section 321 exempt, and pair with CBP First-Sale Valuation for remaining SKUs

Automated 45 CFR § 164.524 HITECH EMR & pharmacy retrieval
LLM ICD-10 / exposure-timeline clinical chronology parser
key_risks: Duplicate or synthetic claimant lead-vendor fraud
State bar unauthorized fee-splitting or runner enforcement
regulatory_notes: Contract strictly at fair-market fixed or cost-plus rates under ABA Model Rule 5.4 Law-Firm MSO agreements (reserving fee-sharing strictly to licensed lawyers or authorized Arizona ABS entities).
Enforce HIPAA/HITECH patient-directed record authorizations, TCPA 1-to-1 consent, and state bar attorney-advertising rules.

inputs: Executed MSO service agreements or verified Arizona ABS licensing documents, state-specific ethics review, fixed/cost-plus rate cards, approved advertising materials, vendor contracts, and an allocation of clinical, legal, and administrative responsibilities.

Documented claimant permission, minimum necessary identifying data, authorized Lexis access and permitted-purpose verification, restricted SSN matching where justified, existing-client indexes, and secure duplicate-review procedures.

Valid patient access requests or medical-record authorizations, provider and EHR inventories, delivery instructions, applicable record-fee rules, privacy/security agreements where required, and a cost ledger for retrieval, processing, and human review.
plays.mechanism: Operate a non-lawyer Management Services Organization furnishing fixed or documented cost-plus marketing, intake administration, duplicate-claimant screening, and medical-record retrieval, while the law firm retains client selection, legal advice, litigation judgment, and settlement control under applicable state versions of ABA Model Rule 5.4 and related advertising and solicitation rules. Alternatively, participate through an actually licensed Arizona Alternative Business Structure within its authorized scope, rather than assuming an Arizona license overrides restrictions in other jurisdictions; non-lawyer MSO compensation must not become impermissible legal-fee sharing or payment for recommendations. Retrieve electronic records under valid patient requests or authorizations and 45 CFR § 164.524 as applicable, distinguishing individual-access fee limits from third-party requests whose treatment differs under HITECH and subsequent case law; the collectible base is earned contractual service fees actually paid, not projected settlements, with record-copying, identity-verification, security, and professional-review costs separately accounted for.
metrics: Collected service economics: paid fixed/cost-plus invoices, receivables aging, and contribution after record charges, identity checks, licensed data access, security, and review labor.
Triage quality: confirmed duplicate rate, false-positive rate after human review, source-linked record completeness, and percentage of files requiring additional patient authorization.
Operational integrity: request-to-record turnaround, overdue access requests, unauthorized-access incidents, and compensation exceptions linked to referrals, settlements, or legal-fee percentages.
plays.name: Rule 5.4-Aligned Law-Firm MSO and Patient-Directed Electronic-Records Triage Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of contracts with outcome-linked compensation, unauthorized legal-decision exceptions, jurisdictional licensing gaps, and record requests missing verified authority.
platform_risks.failure_mode: An administrative services arrangement drifts into prohibited fee sharing, paid recommendations, unauthorized legal practice, or unauthorized health-record access.
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend the affected activity, refer legal decisions to licensed counsel, correct pricing and marketing under ethics review, restrict improperly obtained records, and resume only services supported by valid contracts, permissions, and jurisdictional authority.
platform_risks.impact: The law firm and operator face disciplinary, licensing, privacy, contractual, and collection exposure, while affected records and invoices may require remediation.
platform_risks.trigger: Compensation becomes settlement-linked, marketing promises legal outcomes, staff make legal eligibility decisions, Arizona licensing is treated as nationwide permission, or records are requested without a valid authority pathway.

workflow: 1. Choose and document the operating structure with qualified ethics counsel: use a fixed/cost-plus MSO without prohibited ownership or fee sharing, or obtain the required Arizona ABS license before operating as one; review every jurisdiction served and preserve lawyers' independent judgment.

2. Run approved marketing and administrative intake without selling legal recommendations or making merits determinations; match permitted claimant identifiers against authorized internal and Lexis records, minimize SSN exposure, and send possible duplicates or conflicts to the firm's designated reviewer.

3. Submit properly scoped patient requests or authorizations and distinguish patient access from third-party disclosure pathways; apply the relevant fee rules and, for requests governed by § 164.524, track its 30-calendar-day response period and permitted single extension with written notice, while checking shorter applicable state deadlines.

4. Deduplicate and organize received records into source-linked timelines for lawyer review, restrict access and retention, and invoice documented fixed or cost-plus services independently of settlement size, legal fees, or outcome; reconcile service payments against actual delivery costs.

plays.name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates
plays.mechanism: Pairing an Arizona Alternative Business Structure (ABS) or co-counsel law firm with an institutional litigation-finance credit facility to acquire, medically verify (via $6.50 HITECH patient-directed record requests), and package 1,000–25,000 retained mass-tort plaintiffs (PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, defective medical devices) at $1,200–$2,500 CAC—either flipping vetted case tranches to litigation-finance hedge funds at 2.5x–4x cost or holding for 35–40% global MDL settlement fee splits.
inputs: Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation (JPML) docket analytics, FDA FAERS adverse-event spikes, and EPA contaminant zip-code maps
Arizona ABS / co-counsel retainer infrastructure with e-sign intake and automated HITECH Act (45 CFR § 164.524) medical-record retrieval engine
Non-recourse litigation-finance warehouse credit facility and MDL leadership co-counsel placement contracts
workflow: Identify emerging MDL mass torts with clear causation biomarkers (specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes + geographic/product exposure proof) and deep-pocket corporate defendants
Run hyper-targeted CTV, paid social, and public-record outbound campaigns to sign injured claimants directly onto joint co-counsel retainer agreements

Execute automated HITECH patient-directed electronic medical record (EMR) pulls at the federal statutory cap (~$6.50/record) and use LLM clinical parsers to verify qualifying diagnosis and exposure dates within 72 hours

Securitize verified, deficiency-free case tranches into litigation-finance buyout facilities at $4,500–$9,000 per vetted retainer or hold on the balance sheet for $25,000–$80,000+ gross contingency fees at MDL settlement
metrics: All-in cost per medically verified, deficiency-free retained plaintiff ($1,200–$2,500)
HITECH medical-record retrieval turnaround time (hours) and clinical qualification pass rate (%)
Secondary docket tranche sale multiple (2.5x–4.0x CAC) or net MDL settlement IRR

platform_risks.failure_mode: Daubert general-causation dismissal in the MDL or fraudulent duplicate claimant intake
platform_risks.trigger: Federal MDL judge excluding plaintiff expert witnesses under Rule 702 or lead vendors submitting synthetic/dual-represented claimants
platform_risks.impact: Write-down of single-tort docket value or MDL leadership rejecting duplicate retainers
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time SSN/lexis duplicate-retainer cross-check, immediate HITECH EMR verification before media payout, and max 20% capital concentration in any single MDL
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders

plays.name: Arizona ABS Law-Firm Ownership & Survivor/Mass-Tort Co-Counsel Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Leverage Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1(c) and ACJA § 7-209 (which abolished ABA Rule 5.4 in Arizona via Alternative Business Structure [ABS] licensing) so non-lawyer acquisition operators can legally own an Arizona law firm, acquire inbound institutional sexual assault survivor claims (juvenile detention facilities, rideshare MDLs, clergy/boarding-school/medical lookback windows) and catastrophic mass torts, and participate in lawful co-counsel contingency fee splits ($50k–$400k+ per settled case) instead of capped flat marketing fees.
inputs: Arizona Supreme Court ABS license + designated Compliance Lawyer (ACJA § 7-209)
Trauma-informed inbound acquisition funnels for state sexual-assault lookback windows & federal MDLs
24/7 HIPAA-compliant survivor intake, facility/ride-receipt verification, & national trial co-counsel network
workflow: Form or partner with a licensed Arizona ABS law firm with an appointed Arizona-bar Compliance Lawyer to legally bridge digital acquisition and legal representation
Run empathetic, 100% inbound survivor-advocacy campaigns across open statutory lookback windows (juvenile detention centers, Uber/Lyft rideshare MDL 3084, institutional/youth-facility abuse)

Execute trauma-informed intake, verify facility/detention/rideshare records, and co-counsel with specialized trial litigators under Rule 1.5(e) joint-responsibility agreements to share in back-end settlement fees
metrics: Cost per signed & record-verified survivor retainer ($1,200–$3,500 media cost)
Facility/rideshare corroboration pass rate (%) & zero-fraud docket quality
Realized co-counsel contingency fee per settled case ($50,000–$400,000+ vs. $3k lead sale)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Cross-jurisdictional Rule 5.4 fee-splitting challenges, MDL claimant-fraud rejections, or 24–48 month settlement lockup
platform_risks.trigger: Splitting fees in non-ABS jurisdictions without genuine legal services/joint responsibility by ABS attorneys, accepting unverified lead-brokered retainers, or undercapitalizing multi-year MDL hold times
platform_risks.impact: Disallowance of co-counsel fee division in restrictive states, court dismissal of uncorroborated claims, or working-capital exhaustion before settlement payout
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% primary-record corroboration rate (detention/medical/ride logs) and state-by-state Rule 1.5(e)/5.4 ethics opinion sign-off
platform_risks.fallback: Ensure licensed ABS attorneys perform substantive legal intake/case-work or pair with an MSO (Management Services Organization) structure in restrictive states, enforce strict primary-document verification before filing, and blend fast-settling single-event injury cases with multi-year institutional dockets

inputs: Authorized inbound traffic sources, accurate ads and landing pages, versioned recipient-specific disclosures, TrustedForm or Jornaya evidence where applicable, suppression records and permitted recording notices.

Ringba or Retreaver configuration, documented buyer ping-post endpoints, buyer authorization or licensing checks, vertical-specific eligibility rules, capacities and payout terms including any 90–120-second duration threshold.
Traffic cost data, call-detail records, transfer and consent events, buyer acceptance receipts, duplicate identifiers, dispute reason codes and restricted-access retention settings.
plays.mechanism: Use Ringba or Retreaver-supported routing and buyer integrations to auction qualified inbound calls through sub-second ping-post trees, earning the spread between accepted buyer payouts and traffic acquisition costs. Operate separate programs for ACA/Medicare, auto/home insurance, mass-tort legal intake and emergency home services, with recipient-specific consent where required, sector-specific transfer restrictions and privacy-minimized bid payloads. TrustedForm or Jornaya records can support evidence of the actual named-recipient disclosure but do not independently establish valid consent; negotiated 90–120-second duration triggers qualify payment only alongside genuine caller intent, buyer acceptance and applicable contract terms.
metrics: Net contribution per qualified call: collected buyer revenue minus acquisition, telephony, routing, verification and refund costs.
Routing quality: p95 auction latency, accepted-connection rate, abandonment rate and buyer capacity rejection rate by vertical.
Evidence and dispute quality: percentage of transfers with required recipient-specific permission records, duplicate rate, complaint rate and payout reversal rate.
plays.name: Consent-Verified Inbound RTB Pay-Per-Call Exchange Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Consent-recipient mismatch count, complaint and reversal rates by source, and anomalous clustering of call endings immediately after the billing threshold.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A buyer or routing platform rejects calls or suspends the program because consent, marketing representations or traffic quality fails applicable requirements.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected sources and transfers, preserve evidence securely, refund invalid billings and resume only with corrected disclosures, permitted compensation structures and verified buyer acceptance.
platform_risks.impact: Payout reversals, account suspension, consumer complaints and potential regulatory or contractual exposure.
platform_risks.trigger: Recipient mismatches, misleading ACA/Medicare advertising, restricted legal-referral fee structures, excessive duplicates or calls padded to cross a duration threshold.

workflow: 1. Approve legitimate traffic sources and buyer contracts, segregate verticals, and establish how each caller receives accurate recipient disclosures without misleading benefit claims or prohibited steering.

2. Screen intent, geography, duplicates and applicable transfer restrictions; obtain required permission before transmitting personal information and send only permitted minimal qualification metadata in bid requests.

3. Run the supported sub-second auction with timeouts and capacity checks, identify the selected recipient and obtain any required recipient-specific permission before transfer, then connect the caller without artificially extending duration.
4. Reconcile buyer acceptance and any 90–120-second billing condition against call records, resolve disputes, suppress invalid sources and settle only genuine, contract-qualified calls.

plays.name: Social-to-Search Ad Feed & Ping-Post Lead Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Buy $0.05–$0.12 curiosity clicks on Meta, TikTok, NewsBreak, and native ad networks and route them through a 4-question qualification bridge—replacing fragile $1.50 RSOC/AFD search-feed clicks with direct $45–$180 Ping-Post lead auctions.
inputs: Low-CPC social/native ad hooks ($0.05–$0.12 CPC)
Fast 4-question conditional qualification quiz + TCPA consent capture
Real-time Ping-Post lead distribution engine (Boberdoo / Leadspedia / Phonexa) + RSOC downsell feed
workflow: Acquire low-cost social and native clicks using compliant consumer-benefit hooks (tax appeals, solar rebates, insurance audits, surplus claims)
Pre-qualify zip code, homeowner/business status, and urgency inside a zero-friction 4-step quiz bridge
Auction verified exclusive leads in real time via Ping-Post for $45–$180/lead and monetize non-qualifying traffic via compliant secondary search/affiliate offers
metrics: Effective media cost per qualified lead (CPL) vs. Ping-Post auction payout
Ping-to-Post acceptance rate (%) and sub-500ms auction response time
Net arbitrage margin after ad spend and buyer returns

platform_risks.failure_mode: Ad-account ban, RSOC/AFD feed termination, or TCPA consent challenge
platform_risks.trigger: Using fake 'government stimulus' ad bait, forcing accidental ad clicks, or selling leads without one-to-one TCPA consent logs
platform_risks.impact: Ad account suspension, feed clawbacks, or buyer lead rejections
platform_risks.detection_metric: Ad disapproval rate, buyer return rate >5%, and TrustedForm/Jornaya certificate match rate (100% required)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce 100% factual ad hooks, log cryptographic TrustedForm/Jornaya session certificates on every form submit, and diversify across 5+ direct lead buyers

plays.name: TCPA Serial-Plaintiff Docket Scraping & Real-Time Litigator-Scrub Firewall Tollbooth
plays.mechanism: Offer consent-first outbound compliance screening using lawful docket-derived risk signals alongside mandatory do-not-call and revocation checks; plaintiff matching neither authorizes contact nor replaces TCPA compliance.
inputs: Permitted public docket data with identity confidence scores
Consent provenance, revocations, and suppression lists
Applicable calling rules and customer retention policies
workflow: 1. Ingest permitted docket records with source dates, minimization, and human identity review
2. Check consent, do-not-call status, revocations, and calling restrictions before optional risk enrichment
3. Suppress noncompliant contacts and route uncertain matches to review without planting honeypots or provoking claims
4. Serve auditable screening decisions with correction, deletion, and retention controls
metrics: Contacts blocked for missing consent or suppression match
False-positive identity match rate
Screening latency and stale-record share

platform_risks.failure_mode: False identity match or false assurance of permission to call
platform_risks.trigger: Stale docket data or treating absence from a plaintiff list as consent
platform_risks.impact: Unlawful outreach, privacy complaints, and customer liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: Consent-audit failure rate and upheld identity correction requests
platform_risks.fallback: Disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks

plays.name: CIPA Wiretap-Pixel & VPPA Statutory Privacy-Demand Settlement Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Support counsel-led evaluation of genuine tracking-related privacy claims using preserved consent and disclosure evidence; applicability, standing, and recoverable damages require individual legal review.
inputs: Client-authorized browser network captures
Timestamped consent flows and privacy notices
Counsel-reviewed standing and statutory applicability checklist
workflow: 1. Obtain client authorization and preserve ordinary-session tracking and consent evidence
2. Have counsel assess actual disclosures, statutory coverage, standing, and limitation periods
3. Route substantiated matters to retained counsel for proportionate notice and resolution
4. Record outcomes, client distributions, and remediation without duplicate or fabricated claims
metrics: Counsel-validated matters per reviewed session
Net client recovery after disclosed costs
Evidence completeness and duplicate-claim rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Unsupported statutory demand or evidence rejection
platform_risks.trigger: Missing standing, valid consent, or unreliable attribution of disclosed data
platform_risks.impact: Dismissal, sanctions exposure, and wasted case costs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Counsel rejection rate by coverage and evidence defect
platform_risks.fallback: Close unsupported matters and offer authorized privacy-remediation audits instead

plays.name: Paid-to-Organic Media Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Acquire underpriced clicks from secondary ad networks, newsletter sponsorships, and long-tail search queries, then monetize the spread via higher-yield B2B lead sales, high-ticket affiliate payouts, and organic retargeting loops.
inputs: Low-CPC ad & sponsorship inventory
High-RPM / high-CPL monetization endpoints
Cohort ROAS & LTV attribution ledger
workflow: Buy targeted traffic where CPC is priced below the realized first-session + 30-day email value
Segment incoming visitors via instant qualification prompts to route high-value leads to premium buyers
Recycle organic search and newsletter return visits at zero marginal media cost
metrics: Day-1 vs. Day-30 ROAS spread
Realized RPM minus effective CPC
Lead acceptance rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Traffic-cost spikes, ad-account restrictions, or attribution blind spots
platform_risks.trigger: Auction CPC inflation, ad-network creative disapprovals, or browser tracking restrictions
platform_risks.impact: Negative front-end arbitrage spread and wasted ad spend
platform_risks.detection_metric: Hourly CPC-to-EPC ratio and server-side conversion match rate
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce automated spend circuit-breakers when spread narrows and rely on first-party newsletter monetization

plays.name: Ad-Library Spend-Velocity & Funnel-Clone Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Continuously poll Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, and TikTok Creative Center to detect direct-response creatives kept active >30 days with expanding variant counts, then localize or adapt the proven funnel architecture into untapped verticals and geos.
inputs: Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency, & TikTok Creative Center APIs
Ad-longevity (>30 days active) & creative-variant velocity scoring model
Rapid landing-page localization & multi-geo media buying desk
workflow: Track active ad duration, impression brackets, and landing-page funnel changes across 1,000+ direct-response advertisers
Isolate offers scaling for 30+ consecutive days (proving positive unit economics) and map their quiz/pre-sell mechanics
Deploy original, localized pre-sell funnels in lower-CPM geographies or adjacent B2B verticals—or sell the curated winning-ad intelligence feed to agencies
metrics: Winner identification accuracy (% of cloned architectures profitable in <7 days)
Cross-geo CPM/CPC discount vs. US baseline (%)
Return on ad spend (ROAS) and intelligence-subscription MRR

platform_risks.failure_mode: DMCA takedown, trademark infringement, or ad-account circumvention ban
platform_risks.trigger: Ripping competitor video files/logos verbatim rather than adapting the underlying funnel structure with original creative
platform_risks.impact: DMCA strike, ad-account suspension, or affiliate network removal
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% original creative asset attestation and zero DMCA/trademark notices
platform_risks.fallback: Extract only the structural hook, quiz flow, and offer positioning while producing 100% original copy, design, and video assets

plays.name: Identity-Graph Pixel & Search-Intent Deanonymization
plays.mechanism: Deploy first-party CNAME identity-resolution pixels and pre-click search/bidstream intent feeds (syncing visitor IP/device hashes against publisher co-op SHA-256 rainbow tables and property/B2B graphs) to resolve 35–55% of anonymous bouncing search visitors into verified names, emails, LinkedIn profiles, and physical home addresses.
inputs: First-party CNAME identity-resolution pixel & Google Ads ValueTrack ({keyword}) URL tags
Publisher co-op SHA-256 HEM spine + County Assessor / B2B LinkedIn enrichment graph
Automated physical postcard API (Lob / PostGrid), B2B Slack routing, & Custom Audience sync
workflow: Geo-fence pixel execution at the CDN edge (US-only, excluding EU/UK GDPR traffic) and capture exact referring search keywords via ValueTrack parameters
Resolve anonymous bouncing visitors against the identity spine within 200ms to append homeowner address, work email, and LinkedIn URL
Route resolved B2B executives to instant Slack/LinkedIn warm outreach, trigger physical next-day postcards to resolved homeowner addresses, and sync SHA-256 hashes into Meta/Google Custom Audiences
metrics: Anonymous visitor-to-identity match rate (35–55% target)
Cost per resolved identity ($0.10–$0.25) vs. net recovered revenue per 1,000 bounces
Postcard & B2B LinkedIn intercept conversion rate (%)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Primary email domain blacklisting (>0.3% spam complaint rate) or California CIPA / state privacy demand letters
platform_risks.trigger: Blasting cold consumer Gmail addresses from primary brand domains saying 'we saw you on our site' or firing third-party pixels without geo-fencing/consent notice
platform_risks.impact: Google Workspace / ESP domain suspension or statutory privacy settlement costs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Postmaster Tools spam rate >0.1%, bounce rate >2%, and edge geo-fence block verification
platform_risks.fallback: Never cold-email unconsented consumer Gmail addresses from primary domains; monetize consumer matches strictly via CAN-SPAM-exempt physical trigger mail and SHA-256 ad-audience sync, and enforce US-only edge geo-gating

Direct Supply-Side Platform (SSP) seats and header-bidding wrappers (Magnite, PubMatic, Index Exchange, AppLovin MAX, Google Ad Manager)
Licensed public-domain film libraries, procedural ambient 4K loops, or local weather/news data feeds
workflow: Deploy a portfolio of categorized CTV and mobile apps (e.g., 4K Fireplace/Aquarium ambients, Classic Westerns, Local Radar, Trivia channels) that generate 45–120 minute average session durations

Optimize ad-pod fill rates and floor prices dynamically by household Geo/DMA to capture $18–$35 CTV CPMs
metrics: Net programmatic eCPM ($18–$35) vs. viewer acquisition cost ($0–$2 equivalent CPM)
Average daily viewing hours per active household device and VAST pod completion rate (>92%)
SSP viewability and human-traffic verification score (DoubleVerify / IAS / Pixalate pass rate)

platform_risks.failure_mode: SSP inventory demonetization for 'Made-for-Advertising' (MFA) or idle-screen continuous playback

platform_risks.impact: DSP bid-stream exclusion or app-store delisting
platform_risks.detection_metric: Interactive remote-control heartbeat prompts every 90 minutes and Pixalate CTV seller-trust rating
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce 'Are you still watching?' remote check-ins, maintain clean app-ads.txt chains on every publisher domain, and diversify across 6+ independent SSPs and direct agency PMP deals

Issuer reward categories, caps, and repayment terms
Platform invoices and agency volume-rebate agreements

Unfunded client exposure and repayment coverage
Invoice-to-reward reconciliation variance

Quiz-to-paid conversion and retained subscriber rate
Refund, chargeback, and cancellation completion rates

inputs: Parcel ownership, title exceptions, zoning, access and easement records; utility headroom publications and transmission GIS; fiber-provider route information with written confirmation of serviceability, route diversity, construction cost, and delivery timing.

Project-specific electrical envelopes covering BESS charging and export MW, duration and dispatch constraints, or AI firm load, ramp profile, redundancy, cooling and water requirements; utility study procedures, queue data, upgrade-cost estimates, and written capacity and timing evidence.

Landowner option templates specifying premium, exercise price, 12–24 month term, extensions, assignment consent, diligence termination rights, access for testing, and treatment of deposits; Phase I environmental assessments, wetland delineation needs, floodplain screens, and a qualified developer buyer list.
plays.mechanism: Overlay utility hosting-capacity maps, 69–345 kV transmission corridors, dark-fiber routes, and environmental constraints to originate expressly assignable, diligence-contingent 12–24 month land options. Hosting-capacity maps and proximity are prospecting signals, not commitments: value each option strictly against utility-validated deliverable MW, project-specific import/export requirements, network-upgrade exposure, and a realistic energization schedule. Monetize documented site-control assignments to qualified BESS or modular AI developers, with separate treatment of land rights, interconnection rights, and any utility consent required for a project transfer.
metrics: Risk-adjusted assignment margin = contracted assignment proceeds minus option premiums, extensions, studies, environmental work, legal costs, transaction costs, and probability-weighted failed-site spend; report cash at risk before any buyer payment.

Utility-validated usable MW by import/export service condition, supporting evidence stage, and expected energization date; track the percentage of screened capacity surviving studies rather than presenting map headroom as saleable capacity.
Site conversion and timing: screened parcels to signed options to paid assignments, months of option term remaining beyond expected diligence, and upgrade-cost sensitivity per usable MW.
plays.name: Utility-Validated BESS and Modular AI Land-Option Origination Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Track variance between preliminary and studied MW, upgrade estimates, and energization dates, plus remaining option months relative to utility study and permitting milestones.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Indicative utility headroom is mistaken for deliverable service, leaving an option on land that cannot support the buyer's operating profile within the option term.
platform_risks.fallback: Use the contractual diligence exit or renegotiate price and term before further nonrefundable spending; pursue an alternative operating profile only after fresh utility validation, and withdraw unsupported capacity claims from buyer materials.
platform_risks.impact: The assignment value falls sharply while option premiums, engineering costs, and extension payments become stranded; a land assignment may also fail to preserve separately governed interconnection rights.
platform_risks.trigger: A utility study identifies binding thermal or voltage constraints, a competing service request consumes available capacity, or required upgrades move energization beyond the buyer's investment horizon.

workflow: 1. Rank parcels using corridor, substation, fiber, access, zoning, and environmental overlays; distinguish distribution hosting estimates from transmission deliverability and exclude sites whose apparent capacity depends on unsupported map interpretation.

2. Obtain project-specific utility feedback on import and export capacity, operating restrictions, study requirements, interconnection facilities, upgrades, and achievable energization dates; label screening feedback separately from completed studies and executable service commitments.

3. Execute a counsel-reviewed, expressly assignable 12–24 month option with environmental and utility diligence contingencies, staged payments, extension economics, and clear exercise mechanics; commission Phase I work and necessary wetlands, title, access, and permitting investigations before additional capital becomes nonrefundable.

4. Market a version-controlled diligence package to qualified developers, price the assignment using utility-validated usable MW and schedule-adjusted developer economics, and close through documented assignment and escrow procedures; verify state real-estate licensing rules and separately obtain any required utility or queue-transfer consent.

key_risks: Strict court-seal breach disqualifying relator share
regulatory_notes: File all False Claims Act qui tam complaints exclusively through licensed relator counsel under strict 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2) court seal, and route SEC Form TCR / IRS Form 211 filings through counsel.
Pair long-tail statutory relator upside with recurring B2B forensic data-analytics retainers so operating cashflow never depends on uncollected seal dockets.

inputs: Lawfully obtained procurement, payment, grant, corporate-filing, enforcement, and pricing datasets with acquisition dates, source URLs, applicable use rights, immutable snapshots, transformation code, and a documented separation of public records from any authorized nonpublic evidence.

Counsel-defined investigative hypotheses identifying the relevant payment or securities/tax theory, responsible actors, transaction dates, representations, materiality, estimated loss, alternative explanations, and unresolved evidentiary gaps.

Written analytics engagement covering scope, ordinary service fees, conflicts, confidentiality, evidence retention, and ownership; separate counsel assessments of FCA public disclosure, original-source status, first-to-file and limitations issues, SEC original-information requirements, and IRS submission eligibility.
plays.mechanism: Sell scoped B2B forensic-analytics retainers to contingency relator firms, producing reproducible evidence packages for potential False Claims Act matters under 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3730 and distinct SEC or IRS whistleblower pathways under 15 U.S.C. § 78u-6 and 26 U.S.C. § 7623. Public-data anomalies alone do not establish a knowingly false, material claim or satisfy Rule 9(b); FCA public-disclosure and original-source analysis differs from the SEC's potential recognition of qualifying independent analysis. Treat service revenue as the operating business and any personally eligible whistleblower award as separate, contingent, potentially multi-year proceeds rather than a purchased claim, promised recovery, or share of counsel's legal fees.
metrics: Collected retainer and milestone revenue minus analyst labor, data licensing, expert review, secure storage, and rework; track receivable days and client concentration without booking speculative awards as earned service revenue.

Evidence quality: reproducible transaction coverage, precision on manually reviewed anomalies, documented alternative explanations, and the share of allegations supported by claim-specific facts rather than aggregate correlations.

Program-specific contingent recovery register: FCA shares generally 15–25% with government intervention or 25–30% without, subject to statutory exceptions; SEC awards generally 10–30% of collected sanctions in qualifying actions exceeding $1 million; IRS § 7623(b) generally 15–30% subject to its monetary, taxpayer-income, and other requirements.
plays.name: Public-Data Forensic Analytics and Relator Litigation-Support Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Measure unresolved statutory-element gaps, unsupported claim assertions, source-provenance exceptions, and matters lacking a documented program-specific assessment by counsel.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A compelling statistical pattern is sold as an award-eligible case despite public-disclosure restrictions, insufficient claim-specific facts, or a mismatch between the evidence and the selected whistleblower program.
platform_risks.fallback: Narrow the deliverable to supported forensic findings, preserve exculpatory evidence, and pursue further lawful corroboration only within the engagement; stop unsupported allegations and retain collected service-fee economics separately from any abandoned award thesis.
platform_risks.impact: Dismissal, award denial, wasted litigation expense, confidentiality exposure, and impaired client relationships; paid analytics work does not itself establish relator standing or award eligibility.
platform_risks.trigger: The material is already publicly disclosed or known to authorities, the analyst contributes no qualifying independent analysis or original-source knowledge, or counsel cannot connect anomalies to the required statutory elements.

workflow: 1. Select a narrow, counsel-approved hypothesis and reproduce the underlying transactions from preserved source data; document methodology, false-positive controls, lawful access, and contrary evidence without accessing restricted systems or soliciting privileged material.

2. Build a transaction-level evidence matrix linking alleged conduct to identifiable claims, statements, actors, dates, knowledge indicators, and materiality; have counsel test Rule 9(b) particularity under the governing circuit and assess FCA public-disclosure and original-source issues before characterizing a matter as actionable.

3. Deliver the paid forensic report and reproducible workpapers independently of any award outcome; counsel selects the appropriate pathway, including an FCA complaint initially filed under seal with statutory government disclosures, an SEC TCR submission, or an IRS Form 211, rather than treating the programs as interchangeable.

4. Maintain controlled litigation support, evidence updates, and a docket of counsel-managed deadlines; respect the FCA's initial statutory seal period of at least 60 days and any court-granted extensions, which can extend for years, while forecasting operations from collected retainers rather than expected awards.

platform_risks.fallback: Disable the affected routing, solicitation, or recommendation feature, preserve records, and continue only the lawfully supported read-only analytics or referral functionality; resume expanded activity through an appropriately registered arrangement or a substantiated exemption.

workflow: 1. Confirm each venue's current regulatory status, customer-access model, data rights, and permitted territories; distinguish direct venue access from intermediary access, including ForecastEx access through authorized intermediaries, and verify the current availability of any commercial referral program.

2. Normalize contracts only when their event definitions and settlement mechanics support a meaningful comparison; display bid/ask-derived implied probabilities, depth, timestamps, fees, and settlement differences rather than describing every price spread as executable arbitrage.

3. Launch paid read-only dashboards with stale-data suppression, spread and depth filters, reproducible calculations, and clearly disclosed commercial relationships; assess whether recommendation features create CTA obligations before enabling them.

4. Enable only contractually permitted referral links or a separately authorized routing implementation after documenting the registration or exemption basis; require user-directed orders through the authorized venue or intermediary, minimize token permissions, and retain consent and routing logs without receiving customer funds.

metrics: Realized CPA yield = paid, non-reversed CPA revenue divided by eligible referred visitors; track click-to-registration, verified registration-to-qualifying-depositor conversion, rejection reasons, and the lag between acquisition and cash collection.

Realized revenue share = contractual share percentage applied to the eligible NGR base after agreed deductions and carryover treatment; reconcile the opening negative balance, current-period activity, payable amount, and closing balance by contractual reporting unit.

Jurisdiction-level contribution margin and control quality: content and acquisition cost per paid depositor, cash payback period, blocked ineligible-location clicks, age-screening failures, outdated offers, and operator-authorization exceptions.

Substantiated credits realized by the employer

Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects

All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

economics.owner_net_profit_potential: $28,000–$442,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment
economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Net upfront option/down-payment spreads and retained annual wraparound interest margin; excludes underlying home face value and pass-through debt service
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.

key_risks: Wrap buyer default & foreclosure carrying cost
regulatory_notes: Underwrite every owner-occupant wraparound buyer through a licensed RMLO under SAFE Act / Dodd-Frank Ability-to-Repay rules and state wraparound disclosure statutes (e.g., Tex. Prop. Code §5.016).
Use a licensed third-party loan servicer so underlying mortgage, tax and insurance payments are verified transparently every month.

plays.name: Subject-To Low-Rate Mortgage Acquisition & RMLO-Underwritten Wraparound Note Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Acquire property subject to existing 2.75%–4.25% mortgage debt and, where lawful, resell through an 8.5%–9.9% wraparound note originated with licensed RMLO involvement, applicable ability-to-repay review and licensed third-party servicing. Retain lawful origination economics and the net interest spread rather than operating as a landlord. RMLO involvement does not eliminate due-on-sale acceleration, seller liability, buyer default or property-related obligations.
inputs: Verified underlying loan, title, tax and insurance records with seller disclosures and counsel-reviewed due-on-sale analysis
Qualified buyer file and licensed RMLO underwriting with applicable SAFE Act, Dodd-Frank and state wraparound compliance
Legally reviewed transfer and wrap documents plus licensed third-party servicing, payment verification and default reserves
workflow: 1. Verify the underlying mortgage and title, disclose the seller's continuing debt exposure and obtain counsel-reviewed lender consent or a documented lawful acceleration-risk plan.
2. Underwrite the buyer through a licensed RMLO where required and deliver all applicable consumer, financing and wraparound disclosures.
3. Close only a lawful documented transfer with appropriate insurance and escrow arrangements, assigning property responsibilities explicitly rather than assuming none exist.
4. Service the wrap through a licensed third party, verify underlying debt and tax payments monthly and follow lawful loss-mitigation procedures if payments fail.
metrics: Collected wrap interest less underlying interest, servicing fees and credit-loss provision
Buyer delinquency rate and percentage of underlying payments verified on time
Liquidity reserves relative to acceleration, foreclosure and property carrying exposure

platform_risks.failure_mode: The underlying lender accelerates debt after a subject-to transfer
platform_risks.trigger: Enforcement of a due-on-sale clause or a related servicing or insurance default
platform_risks.impact: Immediate payoff demand, refinancing costs, foreclosure exposure and harm to the original borrower
platform_risks.detection_metric: Lender acceleration notices, unresolved servicing alerts and reserve shortfall against payoff exposure
platform_risks.fallback: Engage counsel and the servicer, pursue lender-approved assumption or refinancing and use a documented lawful sale or payoff exit if necessary

plays.name: Distressed Asset Recovery
plays.mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.
inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers
Unclaimed property & judgment dockets
Surplus auction manifests
workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances
Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value
Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts
metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case
Claim approval rate
Days from filing to disbursement

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold
platform_risks.trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules
platform_risks.impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle
platform_risks.detection_metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required

inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings
County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds
Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline
workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing
Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records
Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions
metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days)
Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%)
Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel

platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges
platform_risks.fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record

Title report and statutory redemption calendar
Local counsel priority and notice opinion

2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions
3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline
4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire
metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs
Capital days outstanding
Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate

Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece

Real-time Pay-Per-Call & exclusive CPL routing switch
workflow: Scrape and normalize daily municipal code citations, failed permit inspections, and recorded mechanic's liens across target metro counties
Enrich parcel owner contact records and classify urgency by abatement deadline or fine accrual rate
Route verified property owners via direct mail/outbound alerts into exclusive Pay-Per-Call or CPL agreements with licensed remediation contractors

Qualified homeowner/commercial call conversion %
Revenue per exclusive routed remediation lead

Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine
Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline

plays.name: Earnest-Money Deposit ("Gator") Escrow Lending & Joint-Venture Splits
plays.mechanism: Advance $2,500–$25,000 refundable-contingency earnest-money deposits directly to title escrow under documented JV or promissory protections, with security recorded or perfected where legally appropriate. Negotiate a 15%–30% share of an earned assignment fee or a lawful fixed return; refunds depend on contractual deadlines, valid contingency exercise and escrow release terms.
inputs: Assignable purchase agreement with explicit refundable contingencies, notice procedures and deadline calendar
Verified title escrow account and executed JV or promissory documents with legally appropriate recorded or perfected protections
Borrower diligence, assignment economics and state-specific lending, brokerage, securities and usury review
workflow: 1. Verify assignment rights, counterparty identity, refundable contingencies and the enforceability of the proposed JV or lending structure.
2. Execute repayment and profit-split documents, perfect any lawful security and transmit the deposit directly to verified title escrow.
3. Track contingency and assignment deadlines, require documented progress and deliver timely cancellation notices when authorized and necessary.
4. Reconcile the closing or refund statement, recover deposited principal and collect only the contractually earned fee or lawful return.
metrics: Earned assignment-fee share or fixed return per completed deposit advance
Percentage of active deposits with verified unexpired refund rights and complete documentation
Deposit loss rate and median days from advance to cleared repayment

platform_risks.failure_mode: A supposedly refundable deposit becomes nonrefundable or disputed
platform_risks.trigger: Missed contingency notice deadline, invalid cancellation or unauthorized contract amendment
platform_risks.impact: Deposit forfeiture, delayed recovery and disputes over assignment proceeds
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deposits approaching contingency expiry without documented assignment or cancellation instructions
platform_risks.fallback: Freeze additional advances, seek timely authorized cancellation and pursue counsel-reviewed escrow release or contractual remedies

plays.name: 24-to-72-Hour Escrow-Locked Transactional ("Flash") Double-Close Funding
plays.mechanism: Fund the A->B acquisition only after the title agent independently verifies cleared, unconditional end-buyer B->C funds in escrow and an enforceable closing waterfall. Target a 1.0%–2.5% earned funding fee per 1–3 day turn; closing delays, fraud and legal restrictions can impair returns or principal.
inputs: Executed A->B and B->C purchase contracts, title commitment and independently verified settlement-agent credentials
Cleared end-buyer escrow funds, written disbursement conditions and a reconciled same-transaction payoff waterfall
Commercial-purpose funding agreement reviewed for applicable licensing, usury and escrow requirements
workflow: 1. Underwrite both contracts, title exceptions, end-buyer closing conditions and the settlement agent's authority and applicable bonding or insurance.
2. Independently confirm end-buyer cleared funds and irrevocable disbursement instructions using a previously verified title-agent contact channel.
3. Wire A->B funding only to approved title escrow after all release conditions are satisfied and the closing sequence is documented.
4. Reconcile B->C settlement, recover principal and earned fees, and release capital for reuse only after cleared repayment is confirmed.
metrics: Earned funding fees as a percentage of funded principal per completed turn
Median and maximum hours from funding disbursement to cleared repayment
Unrecovered principal and delayed-closing exposure as a percentage of outstanding funding

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fraudulent wire instructions or conditional end-buyer funds leave the A->B advance unrepaid

platform_risks.detection_metric: Count of unresolved wire-verification exceptions and funded closings past contractual repayment deadlines
platform_risks.fallback: Stop disbursement, independently reverify settlement instructions and obtain counsel-directed escrow recovery before further funding

High-velocity creative production engine generating 500+ native/social ad variations per week across high-CPC verticals (dental implants, mass torts, solar, auto insurance, HVAC, senior grants)

inputs: US Customs bill-of-lading and HTS duty-spend intelligence identifying mid-market importers paying $1M–$20M/yr in duties via trading companies

Licensed customs brokerage and trade-attorney opinion pipeline

Implement compliant multi-tier invoicing and ERP documentary trails so the customs broker declares the factory's First-Sale price on CBP Form 7501 instead of the middleman's marked-up invoice
Collect a 25–35% contingency fee on all prospective and retroactive (Post-Summary Correction / Protest) duty reductions realized by the importer
metrics: Percentage reduction in declared customs dutiable value (typically 30–50%)

plays.name: DNS/Script Technographic Drop-Off & Renewal-Window Interception
plays.mechanism: Crawl target commercial domains and DNS TXT/CNAME records weekly to detect the exact day a company installs or removes high-ticket enterprise software tags (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, NetSuite), predicting annual renewal windows (Month 10–11) and active vendor migrations.

Historical install-timestamp ledger (calculating 12-month contract renewal windows)
B2B executive contact graph & migration-agency/SaaS partner routing

Route renewal-window and active-churn signals to competing SaaS sales teams, software resellers, and implementation agencies

Outbound reply-to-demo conversion rate on Month-10 renewal targets

platform_risks.fallback: Combine passive DNS TXT/CNAME monitoring with job-posting technographic mentions to confirm true vendor switches before routing

plays.name: SEC Form 8-K, Form D & C-Suite Turnover Trigger Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Parse SEC EDGAR real-time RSS/JSON feeds for Form D (private Reg D capital raises) and Form 8-K (Item 5.02 C-suite departures, Item 1.01 material agreements, Item 2.01 M&A closings) to trigger sub-hour executive outreach before commercial databases update.

Automated filing parser extracting raise amounts, executive names, & signatory contacts
Enterprise recruiting, specialty finance, & B2B agency deal-routing desk

Extract Form D issuers raising $2M–$50M (who immediately deploy capital on hiring, growth agencies, and software) and Form 8-K executive transitions
Deliver tailored briefings to the filing officers and route warm introductions to executive search firms, enterprise software resellers, and B2B agencies

Form D / 8-K executive response rate vs. cold baseline (3–5x lift)
Retainer and placement referral fees generated per 100 filings
