platform_risks.fallback: Enforce token-bucket rate limiting at 5 req/sec and mirror SEC nightly bulk zip archives for historical lookbacks

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)
platform_risks.trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox
platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap

plays.name: Employer Self-Funded ERISA Plan International Specialty-Drug Importation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Contracting with mid-market US employers (100–5,000 employees) operating self-funded ERISA health plans to carve out high-cost specialty biologics and GLP-1s ($6,000–$15,000/mo US PBM list price) and source the identical manufacturer-sealed drugs from licensed Tier-1 pharmacies in Canada, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand at $800–$2,200/mo—waiving the employee's copay to $0 while taking 25–35% of the employer's $50,000–$100,000/yr per-patient savings.
inputs: Department of Labor (DOL) Form 5500 Schedule A/C database identifying self-funded ERISA employers by broker, TPA, and stop-loss carrier
Licensed international pharmacy dispensation network across Tier-1 jurisdictions (Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand) with cold-chain courier logistics
Turnkey ERISA Summary Plan Description (SPD) 'Specialty Drug Carve-Out Amendment' and $0-copay patient concierge portal
workflow: Mine DOL Form 5500 filings to target CFOs and benefits directors of self-funded companies with 150–3,000 covered lives
Audit the employer's anonymized pharmacy claims file to flag the 1–3% of members driving 45–60% of total drug spend (Humira, Stelara, Skyrizi, Dupixent, Enbrel, Ozempic)
Plug in a voluntary $0-copay international personal-importation program alongside the existing TPA, fulfilling 90-day cold-chain prescriptions at 60–80% below US PBM prices
Bill the self-funded employer plan a shared-savings contingency fee equal to 25–35% of verified net claim reduction ($15,000–$30,000/yr per enrolled specialty patient)
metrics: Verified annual specialty-claim savings ($) per self-funded employer group
Net shared-savings fee revenue ($15k–$30k/yr) per enrolled specialty patient
Employee $0-copay opt-in conversion rate (target: >85%)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Incumbent PBM rebate-contract retaliation or cold-chain customs shipment delay
platform_risks.trigger: Legacy PBM threatening to withhold formulary rebates if specialty scripts are carved out, or border clearance delays on temperature-sensitive biologics
platform_risks.impact: Delayed employer onboarding or need for local emergency bridge fills
platform_risks.detection_metric: Cold-chain transit temperature telemetry and net employer savings after accounting for any forfeited PBM rebates
platform_risks.fallback: Target independent TPAs and transparent pass-through PBMs first, combine international sourcing with US Manufacturer Patient Assistance Program (PAP) optimization, and maintain domestic bridge-fill coverage

plays.name: 340B Contract-Pharmacy & Covered-Entity Drug Price Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Partnering with HRSA-qualified 340B Covered Entities (Federally Qualified Health Centers, Ryan White clinics, disproportionate-share rural hospitals) to provide turnkey Third-Party Administrator (TPA) split-billing software, specialty contract-pharmacy fulfillment, and tele-referral capture—buying outpatient specialty medications at 25–50%+ statutory 340B discounts while collecting 100% full commercial insurance reimbursement and splitting the multi-thousand-dollar per-script margin via compliant flat administrative/dispensing fees.
inputs: HRSA OPAIS (Office of Pharmacy Affairs Information System) database of Covered Entities and registered contract pharmacies
340B split-billing / virtual-inventory accumulator software tracking 11-digit NDCs, prescriber NPIs, and patient-eligibility encounters
Licensed specialty/mail-order contract pharmacy network and commercial payer PBMs
workflow: Identify under-monetized 340B Covered Entities (FQHCs, grantees, rural hospitals) with low specialty capture rates in the HRSA OPAIS registry
Deploy split-billing TPA software and mail-order specialty contract-pharmacy infrastructure that captures commercially insured prescriptions written or co-managed by clinic providers
Reimburse the pharmacy at full commercial payer rates ($3,000–$12,000/script) while replenishing drug inventory via the clinic's 340B wholesaler account at $800–$4,000/script
Charge fixed fair-market-value per-dispense administrative, software, and clinical-management fees that capture a major share of the net spread while funding the clinic's safety-net mission
metrics: Captured commercially insured 340B scripts per month per Covered Entity
Gross commercial-to-340B acquisition spread ($1,500–$6,000+) per specialty fill
HRSA audit pass rate (zero duplicate Medicaid discount or diversion findings)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Manufacturer contract-pharmacy restriction policies or HRSA 'patient definition' audit findings
platform_risks.trigger: Drug manufacturers restricting 340B replenishment to a single contract pharmacy unless claims data is submitted, or filling scripts for patients without a documented clinic encounter
platform_risks.impact: Loss of 340B ceiling price on specific NDCs or HRSA repayment liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% EHR encounter-to-NPI match verification prior to 340B replenishment accumulation and automated ESP (340B ESP) data submission
platform_risks.fallback: Operate an in-house entity-owned specialty pharmacy location alongside contract pharmacies, automate 340B ESP claims-data uploads to unlock restricted NDCs, and enforce strict EHR encounter gates

plays.name: Section 321 "De Minimis" & Border Bonded-Warehouse Tariff Split-Shipping Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Routing bulk sea/air container imports for high-tariff DTC and marketplace brands into Tijuana (IMMEX) or Canadian border-zone bonded 3PL warehouses instead of US ports, then fulfilling individual US consumer orders across the border daily under 19 U.S.C. § 1321 (Section 321 Entry Type 86)—legally eliminating 15%–42.5% customs duties on qualifying consumer parcels and charging brands 35–50% of the saved tariff bill plus 3PL fulfillment fees.
inputs: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) database cross-referenced against US Customs Bill-of-Lading import records (ImportYeti / Panjiva / Datamyne)
Nearshore Mexican IMMEX or Canadian customs-bonded fulfillment center 5–15 miles from San Ysidro/Otay Mesa or Windsor/Blaine border crossings
Automated CBP ACE Entry Type 86 manifest software transmitting 10-digit HTS and consignee data per individual consumer parcel
workflow: Scrape public maritime Bill-of-Lading records to identify US apparel, footwear, luggage, and consumer-goods brands importing 20+ containers/yr in 18%–37.5% HTS duty brackets
Divert the client's ocean containers in-bond (IT/T&E bond) directly to the nearshore border-zone fulfillment facility without paying US bulk entry duties
Sync the warehouse WMS with the brand's Shopify/Amazon store so each US consumer order (<$800 retail value, 1 per person per day) is picked, packed, and cleared via CBP Entry Type 86 at $0 duty
Line-item bill the brand for standard pick-and-pack fulfillment plus a 35–50% contingency split of the verified customs duties eliminated
metrics: Annualized customs duty eliminated ($500k–$10M+/yr per enterprise brand client)
Net tariff-savings share + 3PL margin ($) per parcel cleared across the border
CBP Type 86 automated release rate (>99.4%) and border transit time (<6 hours to USPS/FedEx domestic injection)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory exclusion of specific Section 301 country-of-origin SKUs from Section 321 de minimis eligibility
platform_risks.trigger: Executive/statutory rulemaking removing China-origin Section 301 HTS codes from Entry Type 86 eligibility or tightening 10-digit HTS description rules
platform_risks.impact: Loss of Section 321 duty exemption on affected country-of-origin SKUs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time HTS + Country-of-Origin eligibility screen in the WMS before container booking
platform_risks.fallback: Focus on non-301 origin goods (Vietnam, India, EU, Bangladesh, Cambodia) where high MFN duties (16%–32% on apparel/footwear/textiles) remain 100% Section 321 exempt, and pair with CBP First-Sale Valuation for remaining SKUs

plays.name: CBP "First-Sale Rule" (19 CFR § 152.103) Multi-Tier Customs Valuation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Restructuring multi-tiered import supply chains under the US Court of Appeals *Nissho Iwai* 'First Sale Rule' so US importers legally declare the lower factory-to-middleman transaction price ($8) for US Customs duty and tariff calculation rather than the middleman-to-US-importer invoice price ($18)—slashing annual tariff cash outflows by 35–55% across $10M–$250M+ in imported merchandise.
inputs: US Customs bill-of-lading and HTS duty-spend intelligence identifying mid-market importers paying $1M–$20M/yr in duties via trading companies
Three-party contract, factory cost-sheet, and arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation templates satisfying CBP *Nissho Iwai* criteria
Licensed customs brokerage and trade-attorney opinion pipeline
workflow: Identify US importers purchasing finished goods through Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwanese, or European trading intermediaries or sourcing agents
Audit the two-tier transaction chain to confirm (1) bona fide sale from factory to middleman, (2) clear designation for US export at factory order, and (3) arm's-length pricing
Implement compliant multi-tier invoicing and ERP documentary trails so the customs broker declares the factory's First-Sale price on CBP Form 7501 instead of the middleman's marked-up invoice
Collect a 25–35% contingency fee on all prospective and retroactive (Post-Summary Correction / Protest) duty reductions realized by the importer
metrics: Percentage reduction in declared customs dutiable value (typically 30–50%)
Annualized cash tariff savings ($300k–$5M+/yr per importer) and retroactive PSC refund recovery ($)
CBP CF-28/CF-29 Request for Information audit survival rate (100% documentary compliance)

platform_risks.failure_mode: CBP disallowance of First-Sale valuation during a CF-28 Request for Information audit
platform_risks.trigger: Related-party factory/middleman entities failing to prove arm's-length profit margins or refusing to disclose factory commercial invoices
platform_risks.impact: Re-assessment of duties on the second-sale price plus interest
platform_risks.detection_metric: Annual pre-audit verification of factory commercial invoices, bank wire proofs, and OECD transfer-pricing benchmark studies
platform_risks.fallback: Store encrypted factory invoices in a confidential customs-broker escrow vault (so the US buyer never sees the middleman's margin, while CBP auditors have full access) and back every program with a formal customs-counsel opinion letter

plays.name: B2B Commercial Virtual Card (VCC) Interchange & AP Settlement Rebate Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Embedding a 'Free Automated Accounts Payable (AP) / Instant Vendor Settlement' platform inside high-volume B2B verticals (freight brokerage, construction general contracting, medical supply, property management, media agencies) that converts checks and ACH payables into single-use Visa/Mastercard Commercial Virtual Credit Cards (VCCs)—capturing 140–195 basis points (1.40%–1.95%) in uncapped commercial interchange rebates on hundreds of millions in third-party invoice volume.
inputs: BaaS / Commercial Card Issuing bank partnership (Marqeta, Lithic, Stripe Issuing, Highnote, Cross River) on uncapped Visa/Mastercard Large-Ticket & Purchasing interchange tiers
ERP/accounting connector (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, McLeod/TMW freight TMS) ingesting open vendor AP ledgers

County Recorder grant/warranty deed & mortgage recording dockets
Programmatic print-and-mail API (Lob / PostGrid) + QR intake bridge
workflow: Pull daily new-LLC formations (filtering for employer/commercial NAICS or multi-member filings) and newly recorded residential deeds with purchase price and loan metadata
Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data

Monetize new LLCs via recurring annual labor-poster/registered-agent compliance memberships and B2B partner referrals; monetize new deeds via contingency property-tax appeal filings or high-ticket homeowner lead sales
metrics: Filing-to-mailbox latency (hours)
QR scan & intake conversion % per 1,000 mailers
Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece

platform_risks.failure_mode: USPS 39 U.S.C. § 3001(h)-(i) mail-stop order, State AG UDAP enforcement, or payment-processor freeze
platform_risks.trigger: Styling mailers as fake government penalty notices, invoices, or charging $89-$195 solely for a $3 public deed copy without statutory disclaimers
platform_risks.impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates
platform_risks.detection_metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency
platform_risks.fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services)

plays.name: Rank-and-Rent Digital Real Estate & Pay-Per-Call Routing
plays.mechanism: Build and rank local high-ticket service hubs (foundation repair, water restoration, probate liquidation, commercial roofing) wired to dynamic call-tracking switches (Ringba / Twilio) that auto-bill local operators $75–$300 per inbound call lasting over 90 seconds.
inputs: City + high-ticket emergency/specialty service domain portfolio
Ringba / Twilio dynamic number insertion (DNI) & IVR duration billing switch
Co-verified local contractor partner agreements with card-on-file auto-recharge
workflow: Launch fast programmatic local service pages and cost calculators for high-ticket, high-urgency verticals ($5,000+ average job ticket)
Partner with a licensed brick-and-mortar operator in each city for legitimate Google Business Profile co-verification while retaining ownership of the domain and tracking numbers
Route inbound prospect calls through Ringba with a 90-second duration threshold, automatically charging the partner's card on file per qualified call
metrics: Inbound calls per site per month & % of calls >90 seconds
Revenue per qualified call ($75–$300) and contractor retention rate
Portfolio gross margin (80–90% once ranked)

platform_risks.trigger: Registering fake Google Maps pins at UPS stores/virtual offices or delivering calls before collecting prepaid credit balances
platform_risks.impact: Loss of Map Pack call volume or uncollected call receivables
platform_risks.detection_metric: Organic-vs-Maps call split and prepaid Stripe wallet balance per partner
platform_risks.fallback: Anchor traffic in organic city/calculator pages (immune to GBP suspension), co-verify Maps only with real partner physical addresses, and enforce prepaid auto-refill call wallets

plays.name: Identity-Graph Pixel & Search-Intent Deanonymization
plays.mechanism: Deploy first-party CNAME identity-resolution pixels and pre-click search/bidstream intent feeds (syncing visitor IP/device hashes against publisher co-op SHA-256 rainbow tables and property/B2B graphs) to resolve 35–55% of anonymous bouncing search visitors into verified names, emails, LinkedIn profiles, and physical home addresses.
inputs: First-party CNAME identity-resolution pixel & Google Ads ValueTrack ({keyword}) URL tags
Publisher co-op SHA-256 HEM spine + County Assessor / B2B LinkedIn enrichment graph
Automated physical postcard API (Lob / PostGrid), B2B Slack routing, & Custom Audience sync
workflow: Geo-fence pixel execution at the CDN edge (US-only, excluding EU/UK GDPR traffic) and capture exact referring search keywords via ValueTrack parameters
Resolve anonymous bouncing visitors against the identity spine within 200ms to append homeowner address, work email, and LinkedIn URL
Route resolved B2B executives to instant Slack/LinkedIn warm outreach, trigger physical next-day postcards to resolved homeowner addresses, and sync SHA-256 hashes into Meta/Google Custom Audiences
metrics: Anonymous visitor-to-identity match rate (35–55% target)
Cost per resolved identity ($0.10–$0.25) vs. net recovered revenue per 1,000 bounces
Postcard & B2B LinkedIn intercept conversion rate (%)

platform_risks.trigger: Blasting cold consumer Gmail addresses from primary brand domains saying 'we saw you on our site' or firing third-party pixels without geo-fencing/consent notice
platform_risks.impact: Google Workspace / ESP domain suspension or statutory privacy settlement costs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Postmaster Tools spam rate >0.1%, bounce rate >2%, and edge geo-fence block verification
platform_risks.fallback: Never cold-email unconsented consumer Gmail addresses from primary domains; monetize consumer matches strictly via CAN-SPAM-exempt physical trigger mail and SHA-256 ad-audience sync, and enforce US-only edge geo-gating

plays.name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping
plays.mechanism: Parse county probate petitions (Letters Testamentary / Letters of Administration) and daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) filings before national aggregators index them, matching out-of-state personal representatives and distressed owners to licensed probate brokers and cash buyers.
inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings
County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds
Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline
workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing
Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records
Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions
metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days)
Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%)
Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel

platform_risks.failure_mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting
platform_risks.trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits
platform_risks.impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges
platform_risks.fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record

plays.name: Municipal Code-Violation, Mechanic's Lien & Permit-Failure Lead Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Poll municipal building department portals and county recorder dockets daily for failed structural/fire inspections, expired permits, code citations, and newly filed mechanic's liens, routing exclusive real-time leads to remediation contractors and construction attorneys.
inputs: Municipal Accela/EnerGov building & code-enforcement portals
County recorder mechanic's lien & lis pendens dockets
Real-time Pay-Per-Call & exclusive CPL routing switch
workflow: Scrape and normalize daily municipal code citations, failed permit inspections, and recorded mechanic's liens across target metro counties
Enrich parcel owner contact records and classify urgency by abatement deadline or fine accrual rate
Route verified property owners via direct mail/outbound alerts into exclusive Pay-Per-Call or CPL agreements with licensed remediation contractors
metrics: Citation-to-outreach latency (hours)
Qualified homeowner/commercial call conversion %
Revenue per exclusive routed remediation lead

platform_risks.failure_mode: Municipal portal IP blocking or deceptive official-notice complaints
platform_risks.trigger: Aggressive unthrottled scraping of Accela/EnerGov portals or styling outreach like an official city abatement order
platform_risks.impact: Portal IP block or city attorney cease-and-desist notice
platform_risks.detection_metric: Portal HTTP 403/429 rate and zero municipal impersonation complaints
platform_risks.fallback: Use low-frequency scheduled API/bulk exports and clearly identify all outreach as private commercial contractor/remediation assistance

plays.name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.
inputs: Annual county tax-assessor preliminary valuation rolls & parcel GIS characteristics
Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine
Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline
workflow: Ingest county assessment rolls the day annual valuation notices drop and compute each parcel's assessed-per-sqft percentile against direct neighborhood peers
Mail personalized pre-filled protest postcards showing the owner's exact estimated over-assessment and a QR code to sign a zero-upfront-cost contingency authorization
Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings
metrics: Protest-window mail-to-signed-authorization conversion %
Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target)
Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel

platform_risks.failure_mode: State property-tax consultant licensing requirements or missed county protest bar dates
platform_risks.trigger: Representing property owners for a fee without required state registration (e.g., Texas TDLR Property Tax Consultant license) or missing the 30/45-day county filing deadline
platform_risks.impact: Rejected bulk filings, administrative fines, or zero contingency revenue for the tax year
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% licensed tax-agent sign-off in regulated states and T-minus-7-day bulk filing completion
platform_risks.fallback: Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants/attorneys of record in regulated states and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing

plays.name: Multi-Location Google Business Profile (GBP) Local-Pack Grid Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Capture high-margin Google Maps 3-Pack calls across tier-2/3 metros by partnering with real, licensed local tradespeople to co-verify legitimate physical office/shop locations, wiring call-tracking numbers and review-automation workflows to monetize excess lead capacity.
inputs: Geo-grid rank tracker identifying low-review-count Map Pack gaps in $3k+ home/commercial verticals
Joint-venture co-verification agreements with real brick-and-mortar licensed contractors
Dynamic call routing (Ringba) + automated SMS post-job review velocity loop
workflow: Identify suburban and tier-2 metro sub-markets where top-3 Google Maps competitors have <40 reviews and weak category optimization
Sign a revenue-share or pay-per-call partnership with a real local contractor or commercial office tenant (never using fake UPS boxes or virtual coworking addresses)
Optimize GBP primary/secondary categories, service-area pages, and automated customer review requests to lock top-3 Map Pack placement and bill per qualified call
metrics: Local Geo-Grid Top-3 share of voice (%)
Qualified inbound Map Pack calls per location per month
Net revenue per location ($1,500–$6,000/mo) and partner retention

platform_risks.failure_mode: Google Business Profile video-verification failure or network-wide account suspension
platform_risks.trigger: Creating fake storefront listings at UPS stores, virtual offices, or residential addresses without signage/licensing
platform_risks.impact: Immediate GBP suspension and loss of all accumulated reviews and Map Pack calls
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% physical signage, utility bill, and state contractor license verification readiness per profile
platform_risks.fallback: Only launch GBP profiles backed by a real partner's physical shop/yard capable of passing live video verification, and pair every listing with organic city rank-and-rent pages

plays.name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.
inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records
Title report and statutory redemption calendar
Local counsel priority and notice opinion
workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility
2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions
3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline
4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire
metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs
Capital days outstanding
Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien
platform_risks.trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority
platform_risks.impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests

plays.name: GIS Landlocked-Parcel Spite-Strip & Access-Easement Assemblage Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Combine GIS parcel geometry with recorded access rights to option overlooked strips and negotiate voluntary easement assemblages; mapped boundaries alone do not establish legal access.
inputs: County GIS parcel and road layers
Recorded plats, deeds, and easement instruments
Surveyor estimates and neighboring-owner demand
workflow: 1. Flag apparently landlocked parcels and narrow connecting strips in GIS
2. Verify boundaries, existing rights, and easement-by-necessity exposure with surveyor and counsel
3. Secure contingent options and negotiate voluntary access agreements without obstructing existing access
4. Record approved easements and close the assembled sale through title escrow
metrics: Verified access gaps per screened parcel
Option-to-recorded-easement conversion rate
Net assemblage margin after survey and title costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: GIS false positive or unenforceable access premium
platform_risks.trigger: Unmapped easement, boundary error, or preexisting legal right of access
platform_risks.impact: Option expiry or acquisition with no incremental assemblage value
platform_risks.detection_metric: Survey and title exceptions per shortlisted parcel
platform_risks.fallback: Exercise diligence contingencies and offer survey-backed voluntary access services instead

plays.name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing
plays.mechanism: Acquire documented fractional heir interests at a discount reflecting illiquidity, then seek consensual buyouts or counsel-supervised partition subject to heirs-property protections and co-owner rights.
inputs: Probate files and verified heirship records
Title chain, occupancy facts, and independent appraisal
Applicable partition and heirs-property protection rules
workflow: 1. Establish ownership fractions, probate authority, and encumbrances before contacting sellers
2. Provide transparent offers with independent-advice opportunity and modeled partition costs
3. Seek voluntary co-owner buyouts or an agreed market sale before considering litigation
4. If unresolved, use counsel-led statutory procedures honoring notice, appraisal, and buyout rights
metrics: Verified ownership share acquired
Consensual resolution rate
Net proceeds after carrying and legal costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Heirs-property protections defeat assumed forced-sale economics
platform_risks.trigger: Mandatory co-owner buyout, partition-in-kind preference, or defective heirship
platform_risks.impact: Long holding period and lower realizable value
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved heirs and statutory buyout conditions per property
platform_risks.fallback: Renegotiate voluntary exits or retain the interest without threatening unavailable remedies

economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.

inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution
metrics: Cost per verified lead
Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals

plays.name: Industry Award & Verified Directory 'Ego-Bait' Badge Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Publish data-scored state and city rankings ('Top 15 Verified Specialists in [City]') and issue free embeddable 'Top Rated' winner badges to ranked firms—earning hundreds of free high-DR backlinks when firms post the badge on their own sites, while upselling $299–$799/mo Featured #1 Lead-Capture placements.
inputs: Public state licensing, inspection, & review dataset for 500+ firms per vertical
Transparent algorithmic scoring rubric + auto-generated SVG 'Verified Top 10%' embed badges
Self-serve $299–$799/mo Featured Placement & exclusive lead-routing checkout
workflow: Score all licensed operators in a high-ticket vertical using objective public records (years licensed, zero disciplinary actions, review velocity)
Notify top-scoring firms with their free embeddable HTML/SVG '2026 Top-Scored Provider' badge (driving natural dofollow backlinks back to your directory)
Convert 5–10% of shortlisted firms into $299–$799/mo Featured Top-Spot subscribers who receive priority inbound quote requests
metrics: Badge embed rate (% of notified firms linking back to directory)
Domain Rating (DR) growth and organic city-ranking velocity
Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) from Featured Profile subscriptions

platform_risks.failure_mode: FTC endorsement/ranking disclosure scrutiny or Google widget-link spam filtering
platform_risks.trigger: Manipulating objective scores solely for pay-to-play without 'Sponsored' labels or stuffing keyword-anchor links inside badge HTML
platform_risks.impact: Loss of editorial credibility or discounting of badge backlinks
platform_risks.detection_metric: Anchor-text naturalness ratio and clear visual separation of 'Sponsored Featured Partner' vs. algorithmic score
platform_risks.fallback: Keep the underlying algorithmic score 100% objective and immutable, clearly label paid top-spot placements as 'Sponsored / Featured', and use clean branded anchor text in badge embeds

plays.name: SAM.gov / Municipal RFP Scraping & Prime-Subcontractor Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Scrape federal SAM.gov, state procurement portals, and municipal bid boards for low-bid-density service solicitations (janitorial, grounds, courier, translation, IT staffing), pairing compliant proposal automation with vetted local fulfillment subcontractors for a 15–30% management spread.
inputs: SAM.gov Contract Opportunities API & state/municipal e-procurement feeds
Historical FPDS award pricing benchmark database
Vetted local subcontractor network with FAR limitation-on-subcontracting compliance
workflow: Screen daily federal, state, and municipal RFPs/RFQs with <3 historical bidders and clear unit-price schedules
Benchmark winning historical unit rates via FPDS/FOIA award records and lock in binding back-to-back quotes from insured local operators
Submit compliant bid packages and manage billing, insurance, and QA reporting while retaining a 15–30% prime-management or authorized broker spread
metrics: Bid-to-award win rate (%) on low-competition solicitations
Net prime-to-subcontractor gross margin (15–30% target)
Contract renewal / option-year retention rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting) violation or illegal pass-through scheme
platform_risks.trigger: Bidding small-business set-aside contracts and subcontracting 100% of the work to non-similarly-situated entities without performing required prime share
platform_risks.impact: Contract termination for default, False Claims Act liability, or SAM.gov debarment
platform_risks.detection_metric: Subcontracted labor-cost percentage strictly within FAR 52.219-14 limits (<=50% for services unless partnering with similarly situated small businesses)
platform_risks.fallback: Bid unrestricted commercial/municipal contracts without set-aside caps, or team exclusively with 'similarly situated entities' under 13 CFR § 125.6

plays.name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic)
plays.mechanism: Scraping federal DOE/EPA interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries to originate transferable tax credits (IRC § 6418 Clean Energy Investment/Production Credits, Georgia/Louisiana Film Credits, State Historic Rehab & Brownfield Credits) from cash-strapped project developers at $0.82–$0.88 on the dollar and flipping them in simultaneous escrow closings to corporate and HNW taxpayers at $0.92–$0.96 on the dollar.
